docs.title: Overview
docs.text:
StackVet

Universal Project Health & Static Diagnostics Engine Analyze Node.js, TypeScript, and Python projects for broken dependencies, runtime drift, framework pitfalls, and architectural problems in milliseconds.

stackvet is a high-performance, polyglot diagnostic and project health engine for modern stacks (Node.js/TypeScript, Python, Docker, and CI/CD). It inspects your project manifests (package.json, pnpm-lock.yaml, package-lock.json, yarn.lock, pyproject.toml, requirements.txt, uv.lock), active runtime environments, source code ASTs, and infrastructure definitions in milliseconds to uncover broken dependencies, undeclared packages, circular import loops, and runtime drift.

docs.title: Architecture & Internal Design
docs.text: stackvet is built as an offline-first, modular diagnostic engine designed to analyze Python project ecosystems in sub-second execution time.

docs.title: 1. System Overview
docs.text:
Traditional linters inspect only individual source files (AST), while package managers typically only inspect lockfiles. stackvet bridges this gap by unifying four distinct layers of the Python ecosystem into an immutable diagnostic model:

  1. Manifests: pyproject.toml, requirements.txt, setup.cfg, Pipfile.
  2. Active Environment: sys.executable, site-packages, importlib.metadata distributions, and installed version constraints.
  3. Source Code AST: Module import references, circular call loops, and orphan files.
  4. Runtime & Infrastructure: Dockerfile, docker-compose.yml, and .github/workflows/ CI matrices.

docs.title: 3. Subsystem Analyzers
docs.text: All diagnostic checks are implemented as independent analyzers under src/stackvet/analyzers/. Each analyzer accepts the immutable ProjectContext and yields structured Diagnostic instances.

docs.title: 3.1 Dependencies Analyzer (src/stackvet/analyzers/dependencies/)
docs.text:
• Constraint Conflict Engine: Validates installed package versions against declared PEP 508 version specifiers.
  • Missing Dependency Detection: Identifies third-party packages imported in source code that are missing from pyproject.toml or requirements files.
  • Unused Dependency Detection: Pinpoints direct declared dependencies that are never referenced across project source files.
  • Standard Library Awareness: Includes exhaustive Python 3.10–3.13 stdlib catalogs (accounting for PEP 594 removals).

docs.title: 3.2 Environment & Drift Analyzer (src/stackvet/analyzers/environment/)
docs.text:
• Python Version Drift: Compares the active virtualenv interpreter version against requires-python or target runtime.
  • Container Drift: Scans Dockerfile and compose.yml for base image Python version tags that diverge from project targets.
  • CI Matrix Drift: Verifies that GitHub Actions matrix definitions cover the Python versions declared in project manifests.

docs.title: 3.3 Imports & AST Analyzer (src/stackvet/analyzers/imports/)
docs.text:
• Circular Import Cycle Detection (IMP-001): Constructs a directed module dependency graph and uses Tarjan's Strongly Connected Components (SCC) algorithm to identify recursive import loops.
  • Unresolved Local Imports (IMP-002): Flags imports that reference non-existent local packages or missing __init__.py files.
  • Orphan / Dead File Detection (IMP-003): Identifies Python modules that are never imported by any other module, test file, or console script entry point.
  • Architecture Layer Violation Detection (ARC-001): Identifies downward layer skipping (e.g., API directly importing Database bypassing intermediate Services) and upward inverted dependencies.
  • Circular Component Cycles (ARC-002): Traces cyclic dependencies between high-level architectural layers (e.g. Services → Utils → Services).

docs.title: 3.4 Packaging Analyzer (src/stackvet/analyzers/packaging/)
docs.text:
• PEP 621 Schema Validation: Ensures required tables ([project], name, version) are present and syntactically valid.
  • Build Backend Consistency: Verifies configuration compatibility with standard build tools (setuptools, flit_core, hatchling, poetry.core, pdm.backend).

docs.title: 4. Immutable Core Models
docs.text: All state within stackvet flows through immutable, strictly typed dataclasses defined in src/stackvet/core/:

docs.title: 4.1 ProjectContext
docs.text: A frozen snapshot of discovered project assets: - root_dir: Absolute project path. - manifest: Parsed pyproject.toml or requirements metadata. - environment: Active Python interpreter version, virtualenv path, and installed distributions. - source_files: Parsed AST trees and imported module sets. - config: User configuration loaded from [tool.stackvet].

docs.title: 4.2 Diagnostic
docs.text: A structured diagnostic finding: - rule_id: Stable identifier (e.g. DEP-001, IMP-001). - title: Short human-readable summary. - severity: ERROR, WARNING, INFO. - message: Specific description of the root cause. - location: Optional file path and line number. - evidence: Bulleted list of facts discovered during analysis. - suggestions: Recommended CLI commands or code modifications. - fix_action: Optional automated remediation plan.

docs.title: 5. Root Cause Engine & Health Scoring
docs.text:
stackvet computes an objective, deterministic project health score on a scale from 0 to 100:

$$\text{Health Score} = \max\left(0, 100 - \sum_{d \in \text{Unique Findings}} \text{SeverityPenalty}(d)\right)$$

docs.title: 5.1 Severity Scoring Weights
docs.text:
Every unique finding deducts points based on its severity level:

Finding Severity Penalty Points Rationale & Description Behavior in CI Mode (stackvet check) CRITICAL -20 points Catastrophic system failures, event-loop blocking calls in async handlers, fatal runtime breaks. Fails scan immediately (exit code 1). ERROR -8 points Definite runtime breakages, missing package declarations, unresolved imports, cyclic architecture dependencies. Fails scan immediately (exit code 1). WARNING -2 points Transitive dependency risks, unpinned versions, lockfile drift, framework anti-patterns. Fails scan if --strict is enabled. INFO 0 points Informational observations and architecture insights; non-penalizing. Advisory only. HINT 0 points Contextual suggestions and best-practice recommendations; non-penalizing. Advisory only.

docs.title: 5.2 Letter Grade Scale
docs.text:
The numerical health score translates directly into four clear letter grades:

Score Bracket Grade Label Status Description 90 – 100 Grade A A (Healthy) Pristine or near-pristine codebase; zero critical issues and minimal non-blocking warnings. 75 – 89 Grade B B (Fair) Functioning project with minor lockfile drift, unpinned versions, or unused dependencies. 50 – 74 Grade C C (Degraded) Multiple missing dependencies or framework anti-patterns that need remediation. 0 – 49 Grade F F (Critical Issues) Severe architectural defects, blocking synchronous calls, or missing direct dependencies.

docs.title: 5.3 Deterministic Scoring & Zero-Distortion Deduplication
docs.text:
To ensure that repeated scans produce consistent results without score drift:

  1. Deterministic Discovery & Analysis: All discovered source files, manifests, and Dockerfiles are sorted lexicographically prior to AST and dependency traversal. Analyzers iterate through dependency maps via ordered trees (BTreeMap), eliminating random hash iteration variances.
  2. Finding Deduplication: Diagnostics are deduplicated by composite key (rule_id, file_path, line, message). If multiple analyzers or repeated passes flag the same underlying finding, duplicate occurrences are suppressed and recorded as ignored duplicates, preventing redundant penalties from distorting the health score.
  3. Total Deterministic Diagnostic Ordering: All emitted diagnostics are sorted by:
  4. Primary: severity descending (CRITICAL > ERROR > WARN > INFO > HINT)
  5. Secondary: rule_id ascending
  6. Tertiary: file_path ascending
  7. Quaternary: line ascending
  8. Quinary: message ascending

docs.title: 5.4 Score Explainability & Attribution
docs.text:
stackvet provides full transparency into how the health score is derived:

  • CLI Breakdown (stackvet doctor --explain): Emits a formatted attribution scorecard listing the exact deductions per rule and an itemized table of contributing diagnostics.
  • Structured JSON (--json): Includes the complete score_breakdown object (HealthScoreExplanation), detailing base_score, final_score, total_deductions, unique_findings_count, duplicate_findings_ignored, rule_contributions, and itemized diagnostic_details.
  • HTML Dashboard (--html): Embeds deduction metrics and deduplication summary directly into the health score gauge card.

docs.title: 6. Safe Automated Remediation Engine
docs.text:
The remediation engine (src/stackvet/remediation/) adheres to strict safety guarantees:

  1. Non-Destructive AST/TOML Editing: Modifications to pyproject.toml preserve existing formatting, comments, and unrelated tables.
  2. Dry-Run Diff Generation: All proposed fixes can be inspected in advance via stackvet fix --dry-run.
  3. Reversible Fix Actions: Fixes are scoped to specific files with atomic writes.
  4. Package Manager Auto-Sync: When --sync is passed, stackvet automatically invokes the project's native tool (uv sync, poetry install, pip install) to update the virtualenv.

docs.title: 7. Multi-Channel Reporting Pipeline
docs.text:
Diagnostics can be formatted and routed to multiple consumers:

  • Terminal Reporter: Human-readable colorized output with evidence boxes and suggestion snippets.
  • Interactive TUI Dashboard (stackvet inspect): Rich terminal interface with dual panes, scrolling, keyboard shortcuts, and live dependency tree toggling.
  • Standalone HTML Report (stackvet scan --html): Single-file HTML dashboard with SVG health score meters, real-time client-side search, severity filters, and light/dark theme toggle.
  • SARIF v2.1.0 Reporter: Standard OASIS SARIF format for GitHub Advanced Security and Code Scanning alerts.
  • JSON Reporter: Machine-readable output for custom scripts and dashboard ingestion.

docs.title: StackVet Performance Benchmarks
docs.text:
StackVet is engineered with performance and concurrency as core tenets, leveraging multi-threaded traversals (rayon, ignore::WalkBuilder) and native AST parsers (ruff_python_parser, oxc_parser) rather than regex heuristics or subprocess invocations.

This document describes the automated, reproducible performance benchmark suite, how to run it locally, and reference hardware baseline metrics.

docs.title: 1. Benchmark Suite Overview
docs.text:
The benchmark suite is implemented in crates/stackvet-cli/benches/scan_bench.rs using Criterion.rs. It isolates and profiles critical paths:

  1. scanner_directory_traversal_50_files:
  2. Creates a synthetic multi-language project repository with nested directories, .gitignore exclusions, Python files, TypeScript components, and configuration files (package.json, pyproject.toml).

  3. Measures end-to-end multi-threaded directory traversal, exclusion filter evaluation, and context generation.

  4. python_ast_parse_ruff:

  5. Parses modern asynchronous Python source code containing type annotations, docstrings, class definitions, and FastAPI-style endpoint routes.

  6. Benchmarks raw AST construction throughput using the zero-copy ruff_python_parser engine.

  7. typescript_ast_parse_oxc:

  8. Parses complex TypeScript/React code with JSX, hooks (useState, useEffect, useCallback), and TypeScript interfaces.

  9. Benchmarks AST parsing speed using the high-performance oxc_parser.

  10. health_scoring_and_correlation_100_diags:

  11. Simulates 100 heterogeneous diagnostics across Python, Node.js, and framework analyzers.
  12. Measures root-cause correlation clustering (CorrelationEngine), graph grouping, deduplication, and health score explanation calculation.

docs.title: Prerequisites
docs.text:
• Rust stable toolchain (1.80+)
  • cargo

docs.title: Execution Command
docs.text:
To run the full benchmark suite:

cargo bench -p stackvet

To run a specific benchmark (e.g., Python AST parsing):

cargo bench -p stackvet -- python_ast_parse_ruff

docs.title: Generated Reports
docs.text: Criterion automatically generates detailed statistical analysis and HTML reports: - Location: target/criterion/report/index.html - Metrics: Mean execution time, standard deviation, p-values, regression tracking against previous runs.

docs.title: 4. Performance Guidelines for Contributors
docs.text:
1. AST-First Principle: Never replace AST traversal with regular expressions for code semantics. AST parsing is both safer and faster than complex multi-line regexes.
  2. Zero Allocation in Hot Loops: Prefer slices (&str, &[T]) over cloning strings or vectors during file scanning and rule matching.
  3. Respect .gitignore: Traversal must always utilize ignore::WalkBuilder with standard exclusions (node_modules/, .venv/, target/, .git/) to prevent scanning unbounded directories.
  4. Pre-PR Regression Checks: When modifying scanner or analyzer logic, run cargo bench -p stackvet to ensure no latency regressions > 10% are introduced.

docs.title: CI/CD Integration
docs.text: stackvet is designed to seamlessly run in Continuous Integration workflows and upload code scanning alerts.

docs.title: 1. Official GitHub Action (inzamol/stackvet)
docs.text:
Use the official composite GitHub Action to run stackvet with automated PR annotations, SARIF reports, and step summaries:

name: Python Project Health Check

on: [push, pull_request]

permissions:
  contents: read
  security-events: write

jobs:
  stackvet-check:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      - name: Run stackvet Health Scan
        uses: inzamol/stackvet@v1
        with:
          format: sarif
          output: stackvet-results.sarif
          fail-on: error

      - name: Upload SARIF to GitHub Code Scanning
        uses: github/codeql-action/upload-sarif@v4
        if: always()
        with:
          sarif_file: stackvet-results.sarif
          category: stackvet

docs.title: 1.1 Action Inputs & Configuration
docs.text:
Input Description Default path Path to the Python project directory to analyze . version Version of stackvet to use (pinned version like 1.0.1, latest, or local) 1.0.1 python-version Python version used to run stackvet (3.10, 3.11, 3.12, 3.13) 3.12 format Output report format (sarif, terminal, json, html, text) sarif output Output file path for generated report stackvet-results.sarif fail-on Finding severity causing workflow failure (error, warning, none) error github-annotations Emit GitHub Actions inline annotations (::error, ::warning) true offline Disable remote vulnerability queries (airgapped mode) false baseline Path to baseline snapshot to ignore existing findings "" args Additional CLI arguments to pass to stackvet scan ""

Tip (Reproducible Builds): For deterministic production workflows, pin the GitHub Action with a full commit SHA in uses: (e.g. uses: inzamol/stackvet@<commit-sha>) and pin the stackvet package using the version input (e.g. version: "1.0.1"), rather than floating on latest. When version: latest is requested, the action resolves the newest release from PyPI and fails clearly if network resolution is unavailable.

docs.text:
Run stackvet directly in your Node.js or monorepo CI without Python or Rust installation:

name: Node.js Project Health Check

on: [push, pull_request]

jobs:
  stackvet-node:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      - uses: actions/setup-node@v4
        with:
          node-version: "22"

      # Run StackVet directly using npx
      - name: Run StackVet Health Scan
        run: npx @inzamol/stackvet scan --ci --github-annotations

docs.title: 2.3 GitHub PR Intelligence (Changed Code & Annotations)
docs.text:
Run PR intelligence on pull requests to analyze only modified lines/files, emit inline workflow command annotations (::error and ::warning), report resolved issues, and generate a step summary:

name: PR Intelligence

on:
  pull_request:
    types: [opened, synchronize, reopened]

jobs:
  stackvet-pr:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
        with:
          fetch-depth: 0 # Fetch git history for base ref comparison
      - uses: astral-sh/setup-uv@v3
        with:
          version: "latest"

      # Analyzes changed code, emits GitHub annotations, and generates step summary
      - name: Run StackVet PR Intelligence
        run: uv run stackvet pr --ci --github-annotations

docs.title: 2.4 Baseline & Differential Scanning (Prevent New Regressions)
docs.text:
For large existing codebases with pre-existing warnings or technical debt, use baseline snapshots so CI only fails on new diagnostic issues introduced in pull requests:

name: CI (Baseline Verification)

on: [push, pull_request]

jobs:
  stackvet-baseline:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      - uses: astral-sh/setup-uv@v3

      # Verify that no new issues exist beyond .stackvet-baseline.json
      - name: Verify StackVet Baseline
        run: uv run stackvet baseline verify --strict

Or pass --baseline to standard scans: 

uv run stackvet scan --ci --baseline .stackvet-baseline.json

docs.title: 2.3 CI/CD Workflow & Dockerfile Auditing
docs.text:
Add targeted health audits to ensure your CI workflows and Docker environments conform to production security best practices:

      # Audit GitHub Actions workflow definitions
      - name: Audit CI Workflows
        run: uv run stackvet ci

      # Audit Dockerfiles and docker-compose configurations
      - name: Audit Docker Assets
        run: uv run stackvet docker

docs.title: 2.4 GitHub Code Scanning with SARIF
docs.text:
stackvet supports emitting findings in SARIF v2.1.0 format for GitHub Advanced Security and Code Scanning:

name: Security & Health Scan

on:
  push:
    branches: [main]
  pull_request:
    branches: [main]

jobs:
  stackvet-sarif:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      - uses: astral-sh/setup-uv@v3

      - name: Run stackvet SARIF scan
        run: uv run stackvet scan --sarif --output results.sarif
        continue-on-error: true

      - name: Upload SARIF report
        uses: github/codeql-action/upload-sarif@v4
        with:
          sarif_file: results.sarif

docs.title: 3. Pre-commit Integration
docs.text:
stackvet provides native pre-commit hooks via .pre-commit-hooks.yaml.

Add this to your project's .pre-commit-config.yaml:

repos:
  - repo: https://github.com/inzamol/stackvet
    rev: v0.1.0
    hooks:
      # Block commits if diagnostic errors or warnings are detected
      - id: stackvet-scan
        args: [--strict, --offline]

      # Optional: Automatically remediate safe issues on commit
      # - id: stackvet-fix

docs.title: 3.1 Available Hooks
docs.text: Hook ID Description Default Command stackvet-scan Runs diagnostic health scan on the project stackvet scan stackvet-fix Automatically fixes safe issues (DEP-002, ENV-002, PKG-001) stackvet fix -y

docs.title: 4. Standardized Exit Codes for CI Automation
docs.text:
StackVet returns predictable exit codes across all commands and output formats (text, json, sarif, html):

Exit Code Classification Trigger Condition 0 Success Scan passed with no findings at or above --fail-on threshold, health score meets --min-score, or all findings are tolerated legacy baseline issues. 1 Findings Violation Findings detected meeting or exceeding --fail-on threshold, health score below --min-score, or new regression findings introduced against baseline. 2 Configuration Error Configuration syntax error in stackvet.toml or pyproject.toml, unknown rule ID in [rules], or unsupported severity override level. 3 Execution / I/O Error Target path does not exist, specified baseline file not found, or filesystem read/write error.

docs.title: 5. Baseline-Aware CI Checks
docs.text: In existing or legacy codebases, failing CI on pre-existing technical debt blocks modernization. StackVet's differential baseline system allows teams to establish a baseline snapshot and fail CI only when new regressions are introduced:

docs.title: Step 1: Establish Initial Baseline
docs.text:
# Record existing issues into .stackvet-baseline.json
stackvet baseline record
Commit .stackvet-baseline.json into your Git repository.

docs.title: Step 2: Enforce in CI
docs.text:
# In CI check: tolerate legacy baseline issues, fail only if new errors are introduced
stackvet check --baseline .stackvet-baseline.json --fail-on error
If developers resolve existing debt, StackVet automatically reports the resolved findings: 
✓ Baseline Verified: No new regressions detected above ERROR threshold.
  (42 legacy finding(s) tolerated)
✓ Resolved: 3 legacy baseline finding(s) fixed!

docs.title: Step 3: Update Baseline When Debt is Paid Down
docs.text:
# Update baseline to remove resolved issues and reflect current state
stackvet check --baseline .stackvet-baseline.json --update-baseline

docs.title: CLI Reference
docs.text: stackvet provides commands for scanning projects, explaining findings, configuring rules, and inspecting specific subsystems.

docs.title: 1. Global Options & Exit Codes
docs.text:
stackvet --help
stackvet --version
stackvet --config <PATH>

docs.title: Process Exit Codes
docs.text:
stackvet uses stable, standardized exit codes across all commands, checks, and output formats (Text, JSON, SARIF, HTML):

Exit Code Classification Meaning 0 Success Clean project, no findings meeting/exceeding --fail-on threshold, health score meets --min-score, or all findings are tolerated legacy baseline issues. 1 Findings Violation Findings detected meeting or exceeding the configured --fail-on threshold, health score below --min-score, or new regression findings introduced against baseline. 2 Configuration Error Invalid configuration syntax, unknown rule ID in [rules], or unsupported severity override level. 3 Execution / I/O Error Target path not found, specified baseline file not found, or filesystem read/write error.

docs.title: 2. Project Configuration (stackvet.toml / pyproject.toml)
docs.text: StackVet automatically discovers project configuration from stackvet.toml, .stackvet.toml, or pyproject.toml under [tool.stackvet].

docs.title: Precedence Hierarchy
docs.text: Settings are resolved deterministically using a 3-tier hierarchy: 1. CLI Arguments (e.g. --fail-on, --strict, --min-score, --baseline) — Highest precedence. 2. Project Configuration File (stackvet.toml / .stackvet.toml / pyproject.toml) — Overrides defaults. 3. Built-in Defaults — Fallback.

docs.title: Configuration Schema
docs.text:
# stackvet.toml or .stackvet.toml
[project]
name = "my-application"
min_score = 80
strict = false

[thresholds]
# Minimum severity that triggers CI failure: "hint", "info", "warning", "error", "critical"
fail_on = "error"
# Minimum health score required (0-100)
min_score = 80

[ci]
baseline = ".stackvet-baseline.json"
fail_on = "error"
strict = false

[rules]
# Override rule severities or disable rules entirely
DEP-001 = "warning"
CEL-001 = "disabled"
ARC-001 = "error"

# Detailed syntax with explicit enable flag
[rules.FAP-001]
severity = "error"
enabled = true

[ignore]
patterns = ["legacy/**", "benchmarks/**"]

[[suppressions]]
rule = "DEP-001"
path = "legacy/**/*.py"
until = "2026-12-31"
reason = "Legacy package migration"

docs.title: 3. stackvet init
docs.text:
Creates only a .stackvet.toml file when one does not exist, leaving any existing file unchanged. Optionally generates a pre-configured CI workflow for GitHub Actions.

stackvet init [PATH] [OPTIONS]

docs.title: Initialize in a specific project path
docs.text: stackvet init ./services/backend

docs.title: Initialize configuration and generate GitHub Actions workflow
docs.text: stackvet init --ci github

docs.title: Preview generated configuration without writing to disk
docs.text: stackvet init --dry-run --ci github

docs.title: Overwrite existing [tool.stackvet] block
docs.text:
stackvet init --force 

> [!NOTE]
> When generating CI workflows (`stackvet init --ci github`), StackVet automatically detects package managers. For `uv` projects (`uv.lock` present), it configures `uvx --from stackvet stackvet scan --ci --github-annotations`, allowing `stackvet` to run in an ephemeral tool environment without requiring `stackvet` to be added as a project dependency. For standard pip projects, it installs `stackvet` and runs `stackvet scan --ci --github-annotations`.

docs.title: 3.1 Arguments
docs.text: Argument Description Default PATH Path to the project root directory . (current directory)

docs.title: 3.2 Options
docs.text: Option Description --min-score <SCORE> Fail CI with exit code 1 if health score is below threshold (e.g. --min-score 85) --explain Displays detailed breakdown and diagnostic attribution explaining health score deductions --strict Promotes warnings to errors (fails CI if any warnings exist) --ci Runs non-interactively with strict mode enabled --baseline <FILE> Filter findings against an established baseline file (ignores pre-existing issues) --json Emits doctor health scorecard and score_breakdown as structured JSON --sarif Emits scan results as standard SARIF v2.1.0 format --top <N> Number of top problems to highlight (default: 3) --format, -f <FORMAT> Specify output format (text, json, sarif, html) --html Generates an interactive, standalone HTML dashboard with health score breakdown --ignore <PATTERN> Glob pattern to ignore from analysis (repeatable) --verbose Print verbose analysis and discovery progress --offline Disables remote vulnerability/CVE queries (airgapped mode) --output, -o <FILE> Writes output directly to a file

docs.title: 4. stackvet scan
docs.text:
Runs full diagnostic analysis on the specified directory.

stackvet scan [PATH] [OPTIONS]

docs.title: 4.1 Arguments
docs.text: Argument Description Default PATH Path to the project root directory . (current directory)

docs.title: 4.2 Options
docs.text: Option Description --strict Promotes warnings to errors (equivalent to --fail-on warning) --fail-on <SEVERITY> Fail CI if findings meet or exceed severity (hint, info, warning, error, critical) --ci Runs non-interactively with strict mode enabled --baseline <FILE> Filter findings against an established baseline file (ignores pre-existing issues) --update-baseline Update baseline file with current findings and remove resolved issues --ignore <PATTERN> Glob pattern to ignore from analysis (repeatable) --verbose Print verbose analysis and discovery progress --json Emits scan results as structured JSON --sarif Emits scan results as standard SARIF v2.1.0 format --format, -f <FORMAT> Specify output format (json, sarif, html, terminal, text) --html <FILE> Generates an interactive, standalone HTML dashboard --github-annotations Emits GitHub Actions inline PR workflow annotations --offline Disables remote vulnerability/CVE queries (airgapped mode) --hide-warnings, -W Suppresses warning diagnostics from terminal output --errors-only, -E Only shows blocking error diagnostics (hides warnings and info) --severity <LEVEL> Filter findings by minimum severity (error, warning, info) --output, -o <FILE> Writes output directly to a file

docs.title: 4.3 Exit Codes
docs.text: Exit Code Meaning 0 Clean project — no blocking errors or warnings 1 Blocking findings detected 2 Invalid configuration or unknown rule ID 3 Analysis or runtime failure

docs.title: 5. stackvet inspect (alias: stackvet ui)
docs.text:
Launches an interactive terminal dashboard (TUI) to navigate findings, expand evidence, view dependency trees, and apply fixes interactively with keyboard shortcuts.

stackvet inspect [PATH] [OPTIONS]
stackvet ui [PATH] [OPTIONS]

docs.title: 5.1 Controls
docs.text: Key Action ↑ / k Navigate to previous finding ↓ / j Navigate to next finding Enter / Space Toggle details expansion f Apply remediation fix for selected finding t Switch between Diagnostics and Dependency Tree view q / Esc Exit interactive explorer

docs.title: 6. stackvet fix
docs.text:
Safely and deterministically fixes detectable diagnostic health issues (e.g., adding missing dependencies to pyproject.toml, creating default configuration schemas, and initializing packaging metadata). Note that unused dependency removals (DEP-003) are marked for manual review to prevent accidental deletion of runtime plugins.

stackvet fix [PATH] [OPTIONS]

docs.title: 6.1 Options
docs.text:
Option Description --dry-run Shows proposed fixes and diffs without modifying any files --diff Shows unified color diff of proposed file modifications before applying -i, --interactive Prompts for interactive confirmation before applying each fix -y, --yes Automatically applies all safe fixes without interactive confirmation --rule <RULE_ID> Filters remediation to a specific rule ID (e.g. DEP-002) --sync Runs suggested package manager install/sync commands

Example:

# Preview proposed unified diffs
stackvet fix --diff

# Apply fixes with interactive confirmation per finding
stackvet fix -i

# Preview proposed fixes in dry-run mode
stackvet fix --dry-run

# Apply all safe fixes automatically
stackvet fix -y

docs.title: 7. stackvet baseline
docs.text:
Manages baseline snapshots (.stackvet-baseline.json) of known diagnostic issues to enable differential scanning in legacy codebases without failing CI on pre-existing debt.

stackvet baseline record [PATH] [OPTIONS]
stackvet baseline verify [PATH] [OPTIONS]

docs.title: stackvet baseline record
docs.text:
Records current diagnostic findings into a baseline JSON file: 

# Record baseline to default .stackvet-baseline.json
stackvet baseline record

# Record baseline to a custom file
stackvet baseline record -o custom-baseline.json

docs.title: stackvet baseline verify
docs.text:
Verifies that no new diagnostic issues have been introduced beyond the baseline, while tracking resolved debt: 

# Verify against default .stackvet-baseline.json
stackvet baseline verify

# Verify failing only on errors (tolerating new warnings or info)
stackvet baseline verify --fail-on error

# Verify in strict mode against a specific baseline file
stackvet baseline verify -b custom-baseline.json --strict

# Verify and update the baseline file to accept resolved and new issues
stackvet baseline verify --update

Option Type Description -b, --baseline <FILE> Path Baseline filepath to check against [default: .stackvet-baseline.json] --fail-on <SEVERITY> String Fail CI if new findings meet or exceed severity (hint, info, warning, error, critical) --strict Flag Promotes warnings to failure threshold (equivalent to --fail-on warning) --update Flag Update baseline file with current findings and remove resolved issues

docs.title: 8. stackvet graph / stackvet graph
docs.text:
Visualizes direct vs transitive package dependencies and internal source module import architecture (with circular import cycles highlighted).

stackvet graph [PATH] [OPTIONS]

docs.title: 8.1 Options
docs.text:
Option Description -d, --dependencies Visualizes direct and transitive package dependencies -i, --imports Visualizes internal Python module imports and circular cycles -r, --risk Annotates dependency tree with functional classifications, AST imports, and risk scores -L, --depth <N> Maximum depth level for the tree (default: 5) --json Emits dependency and import statistics as JSON

Example:

# View full project tree (dependencies and imports)
stackvet graph

# View dependency risk and usage graph
stackvet graph --risk

# View only internal module import hierarchy and circular loops
stackvet graph --imports

# View dependency tree up to 2 levels deep
stackvet graph -d -L 2

docs.title: 9. stackvet explain
docs.text:
Displays detailed explanations, evidence requirements, and remediation instructions for a rule.

stackvet explain <RULE_ID>

Example:

stackvet explain DEP-002
stackvet explain CI-001
stackvet explain DJG-004

docs.title: 10. Targeted Subsystem Commands
docs.text: Run focused checks on specific areas without executing the full scan:

docs.title: 10.1 stackvet dependency
docs.text:
Scans for dependency conflicts, missing imports, unused packages, and version mismatches, or renders an annotated Dependency Risk Graph.

stackvet dependency [PATH] [OPTIONS]

Options: - -g, --graph: Render annotated dependency risk and functional usage graph. - -r, --risk [all|critical|high|medium|low|healthy]: Filter dependency graph by risk level. - -L, --depth <N>: Maximum depth level for the tree (default: 5). - --no-annotate: Render compact dependency graph without multi-line annotation details. - --json: Output scan results or dependency risk graph as structured JSON.

Example: 

# Run dependency diagnostic checks
stackvet dependency

# Render annotated dependency risk graph
stackvet dependency --graph

# Filter dependency graph for critical/high risks only
stackvet dependency --graph --risk high

docs.title: 10.2 stackvet environment
docs.text:
Checks for Python runtime drift between local environment, Dockerfiles, and CI matrices.

stackvet environment [PATH]

docs.title: 10.3 stackvet architecture
docs.text:
Scans source code for circular imports, unresolved internal modules, architectural layer violations (ARC-001), and circular component cycles (ARC-002), or visualizes the project's Architectural Layer Map.

stackvet architecture [PATH] [OPTIONS]
stackvet architecture graph [PATH] [OPTIONS]

Options: - -g, --graph: Render visual architecture layer map and dependency flow. - -f, --format [terminal|ascii|mermaid|dot|json]: Output format for the architecture graph (default: terminal). - --json: Output architecture map as structured JSON. - --strict: Fail with exit code 1 if any architectural layer violations or circular component dependencies are detected. - -o, --output <FILE>: Save generated architecture map or diagram directly to disk.

Example: 

# Run architecture static diagnostic scan
stackvet architecture

# Visualize architectural layer map & flow in rich terminal
stackvet architecture graph
# or shorthand
stackvet architecture --graph

# Export architecture map as GitHub-flavored Mermaid diagram
stackvet architecture graph --format mermaid -o architecture.md

# Export architecture graph as structured JSON
stackvet architecture graph --json

# Fail CI if layer violations or component cycles exist
stackvet architecture graph --strict

docs.title: 10.4 stackvet docker
docs.text:
Audits Dockerfiles and docker-compose configurations for security best practices, root user risks, unpinned base images, sensitive file leaks, and cache optimization (DOC-001 - DOC-014).

stackvet docker [PATH]

docs.title: 10.5 stackvet ci
docs.text:
Audits Continuous Integration workflows (.github/workflows/*.yml) for matrix mismatches, unpinned dependencies, outdated GitHub Actions, missing test/lint quality gates, hardcoded secrets, and missing concurrency cancellation (CI-001 - CI-006).

stackvet ci [PATH]

docs.title: 10.6 stackvet framework (alias: stackvet frameworks)
docs.text:
Runs framework-specific diagnostic rules for FastAPI, SQLAlchemy, Django, and Celery.

stackvet framework [PATH] [OPTIONS]

Options: - -n, --name [fastapi|sqlalchemy|django|celery|sql|all]: Filter analysis to a specific framework (default: all detected frameworks). - --json: Output framework scan results as structured JSON. - --sarif: Output framework scan results in SARIF v2.1.0 format.

Example: 

# Scan current project for all framework issues
stackvet framework

# Scan specifically for FastAPI issues
stackvet framework --name fastapi

# Scan specifically for Django issues
stackvet framework --name django

# Scan specifically for Celery issues
stackvet framework --name celery

# Scan specifically for SQLAlchemy / SQL database issues
stackvet framework --name sqlalchemy

docs.title: 11. stackvet pr (alias: stackvet pr-analysis)
docs.text:
GitHub Pull Request Intelligence engine that analyzes only the changed code in a PR, reporting newly introduced issues versus resolved issues, emitting inline GitHub Actions workflow annotations, and generating PR markdown summaries.

stackvet pr [PATH] [OPTIONS]

Example Output:

Below is an annotated example of a complete stackvet.toml or .stackvet.toml file:

[project]
name = "my-application"
min_score = 80
strict = false

[thresholds]
# Minimum severity that triggers CI failure: "hint", "info", "warning", "error", "critical"
fail_on = "error"
# Minimum health score required (0-100)
min_score = 80

[ci]
baseline = ".stackvet-baseline.json"
fail_on = "error"
strict = false

[rules]
# Simple override syntax: set custom severity or disable rules
DEP-001 = "warning"
ARC-001 = "error"
CEL-001 = "disabled"   # or "off"

# Detailed table syntax with explicit enable/disable flag
[rules.FAP-001]
severity = "error"
enabled = true

# Ignore patterns (glob expressions relative to project root)
[ignore]
patterns = [
    "legacy/**",
    "scripts/generate_*.py",
    "docs/snippets/**",
]

# Configured suppressions with rule, path, expiration date, and rationale
[[suppressions]]
rule = "DEP-001"
path = "legacy/**/*.py"
reason = "Legacy package will be deprecated in Q3"

[[suppressions]]
rule = "SQL-001"
until = "2026-12-31"
reason = "Temporary bypass during query refactor"

[[suppressions]]
rules = ["NDEP-001", "RCT-001"]
path = "frontend/src/legacy/**"
reason = "Exempt legacy react components from strict checks"

docs.title: 2. Configuring via pyproject.toml
docs.text:
For Python projects, you can embed your StackVet configuration directly in pyproject.toml:

[tool.stackvet]
min_severity = "warning"
fail_on = "error"
min_score = 80
ignore = ["legacy/**", "benchmarks/**"]

[tool.stackvet.rules]
DEP-001 = "warning"
CEL-001 = "off"

[[tool.stackvet.suppressions]]
rule = "DEP-001"
path = "legacy/**/*.py"
until = "2026-12-31"
reason = "Temporary migration grace period"

docs.title: 3. Rule Overrides & Disabling
docs.text:
You can customize how individual diagnostic rules are evaluated:

Value Behavior "critical" Treats finding as Critical (-20 health score points, blocks CI if fail_on is critical/error/warning/info) "error" Treats finding as Error (-8 health score points, blocks CI if fail_on is error/warning/info) "warning" / "warn" Treats finding as Warning (-2 health score points, blocks CI if --strict or fail_on = "warning") "info" Informational observation (0 health score points deduction) "hint" Advisory observation (0 health score points deduction) "disabled" / "off" Disables the rule completely; omitted from scans, reports, and health score deductions

docs.title: Validation & Zero False Positives
docs.text: StackVet rigorously validates all rule IDs against the 132-rule catalog: - If an unknown rule ID (e.g. NONEXISTENT-999) is declared in [rules] or [[suppressions]], StackVet exits with Exit Code 2 (Configuration Error) and provides a clear error message. - If an unsupported severity string (e.g. "catastrophic") is provided, StackVet exits with Exit Code 2. - If a suppression entry specifies an invalid ISO date format for until (not YYYY-MM-DD), StackVet exits with Exit Code 2.

docs.title: 4. Ignore Rules & File Exclusions
docs.text: StackVet provides a multi-tiered file exclusion system that prevents scanning irrelevant build outputs, package caches, virtual environments, and generated code:

docs.title: 4.1 Built-in Default Exclusions
docs.text:
By default, StackVet automatically excludes known build artifacts and package dependencies without requiring configuration: - .git - node_modules - target - dist, build, .output - .venv, venv - __pycache__, .pytest_cache, .mypy_cache, .ruff_cache, .tox - .next, .nuxt, .turbo

Root project manifests (package.json, pyproject.toml, requirements.txt, Cargo.toml, etc.) are always discovered and inspected even when build folders exist in the repository root.

docs.title: 4.2 .stackvetignore File
docs.text:
You can place a .stackvetignore file in the root of your project using standard .gitignore syntax: 

# Ignore custom test fixtures and legacy scripts
tests/fixtures/**
legacy/**/*.py
*.generated.ts

docs.title: 4.3 Configuration [ignore]
docs.text:
Add ignore patterns in stackvet.toml or pyproject.toml: 

[ignore]
patterns = [
    "generated/**",
    "scripts/benchmarks/**",
]

docs.title: 4.4 CLI --ignore Flag
docs.text:
Pass repeatable --ignore <PATTERN> flags to exclude patterns for a single command invocation: 

stackvet doctor --ignore "temp_*.py" --ignore "archive/**"

docs.title: 4.5 Exclusion Precedence
docs.text: Exclusions are evaluated using a 4-tier precedence: 1. CLI --ignore <PATTERN> (Highest precedence) 2. Configuration file [ignore] (stackvet.toml / pyproject.toml) 3. .stackvetignore file in repository root 4. Built-in default exclusions (Lowest precedence)

docs.title: 5. Configurable Diagnostic Suppressions
docs.text: When a diagnostic cannot be resolved immediately, you can suppress it via configuration or inline comments. Suppressed diagnostics do not deduct health score points and do not trigger check failures.

docs.title: 5.1 Configuration Suppressions ([[suppressions]])
docs.text:
Suppressions can be scoped by rule ID, file glob pattern, specific line number, and expiration date:

[[suppressions]]
rule = "DEP-001"
path = "legacy/**/*.py"
reason = "Scheduled for cleanup in v2.0"

[[suppressions]]
rule = "SQL-001"
until = "2026-12-31"   # ISO 8601 YYYY-MM-DD
reason = "Temporary bypass while DB query is optimized"

[[suppressions]]
rules = ["NDEP-001", "RCT-001"]
path = "src/legacy/**"
reason = "Legacy frontend components"

docs.title: Expiration Monitoring
docs.text:
When until = "YYYY-MM-DD" is specified, StackVet verifies the expiration date during every scan: - Active suppressions (date not reached): Findings are silenced and tallied in the suppression count. - Expired suppressions (date passed): The suppression becomes inactive. Findings are re-evaluated, and StackVet issues a prominent warning: 

⚠️ Warning: 1 suppression entry(ies) in configuration have expired and are no longer active.

docs.title: 5.2 Inline Comment Suppressions
docs.text: You can suppress diagnostics directly inside Python, JavaScript, and TypeScript source files using comments:

docs.title: Line-Level Suppression
docs.text:
Applies to the exact line containing the comment: 

# Python
time.sleep(1)  # stackvet:ignore[FAP-001]: intentional delay

// TypeScript / JavaScript
import 'legacy-pkg'; // stackvet:ignore[NDEP-001]: intentional legacy import
// or block comment:
useLegacyHook(); /* stackvet:ignore[RCT-001]: legacy hook */

docs.title: Next-Line Suppression
docs.text:
Applies to the immediately following line: 

# stackvet:ignore-next-line[DEP-001]: expected missing package
import optional_feature

// stackvet:ignore-next-line[NXT-001]
export const dynamic = 'force-dynamic';

docs.title: File-Level Suppression
docs.text:
Suppresses all instances of the rule across the entire file: 

# stackvet:ignore-file[DJG-001]: Suppress Django warning across entire file

// stackvet:ignore-file[NDEP-001]: Legacy compatibility wrapper

docs.title: Alternative / Linter Syntax
docs.text: StackVet also recognizes standard alternative directives: - # stackvet:disable=RULE / // stackvet:disable=RULE - # stackvet:disable-next-line=RULE / // stackvet:disable-next-line=RULE - # stackvet:disable-file=RULE / // stackvet:disable-file=RULE - # noqa: stackvet[RULE]

docs.title: 6. Precedence Hierarchy
docs.text:
StackVet resolves settings deterministically using a strict precedence hierarchy:

┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│ 1. CLI Arguments (--fail-on, --strict, --min-score)     │  (Highest precedence)
├─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
│ 2. Project Config (stackvet.toml / pyproject.toml)      │
├─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
│ 3. Built-in Defaults (fail_on = Error, min_score = None)│  (Lowest precedence)
└─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘

docs.title: Contributing to stackvet
docs.text: Thank you for your interest in contributing to stackvet! We welcome bug reports, documentation improvements, new diagnostic rules, performance enhancements, and ecosystem visualizers.

docs.title: 1. Development Setup
docs.text: stackvet uses uv for high-performance virtual environments and dependency management.

docs.title: 1.1 Prerequisites
docs.text:
• Python 3.10, 3.11, 3.12, or 3.13
  • uv installed (curl -LsSf https://astral.sh/uv/install.sh | sh or pip install uv / brew install uv)
  • Git

docs.title: 1.2 Clone & Sync Environment
docs.text:
git clone https://github.com/inzamol/stackvet.git
cd stackvet

# Sync all dependencies including dev, test, and doc tools
uv sync --all-extras

docs.title: 1.3 Install Pre-commit Hooks
docs.text:
Ensure all code meets style and safety checks automatically before committing:

uv run pre-commit install --hook-type pre-commit --hook-type pre-push

You can manually trigger pre-commit checks on all files at any time:

uv run pre-commit run --all-files

docs.title: 2.1 Fast Local Unit Tests
docs.text:
# Run full test suite
uv run pytest

# Run specific analyzer or reporter tests
uv run pytest tests/analyzers/
uv run pytest tests/reporters/
uv run pytest tests/test_tui.py

# Run with coverage report
uv run pytest --cov=src/stackvet --cov-report=term-missing

docs.title: 2.2 Type Checking & Linting
docs.text:
# Lint and format checks
uv run ruff check .
uv run ruff format --check .

# Strict static type checking
uv run pyright

docs.title: 2.3 Multi-Environment Matrix Testing (Tox)
docs.text:
Always ensure your changes pass locally across all supported Python versions and QA environments before opening a PR:

# Run all configured tox environments (py310, py311, py312, py313, lint, typecheck, docs)
uv run tox

# Run specific target environments
uv run tox -e py312
uv run tox -e lint
uv run tox -e typecheck
uv run tox -e docs

docs.title: 3. Architecture Overview
docs.text:
CLI / TUI (click + rich)
                                        │
                                Project Discovery
                                        │
                            ProjectContext (Immutable)
                                        │
         ┌───────────────┬──────────────┴───────────────┬────────────────┐
   Dependencies    Environment                      Imports          Packaging
     Analyzer        Analyzer                       Analyzer          Analyzer
         └───────────────┼──────────────────────────────┴────────────────┘
                                        │
                                 AnalysisEngine
                                        │
                                Diagnostic Model
                                        │
                              Root Cause Correlator
                                        │
    ┌──────────────┬─────────────┼─────────────┬──────────────┬──────────────┐
 Terminal         JSON         SARIF         HTML         GitHub Actions   Interactive
 Reporter       Reporter     Reporter      Reporter         Annotator      TUI Dashboard
  • src/stackvet/core/: Core immutable models (ProjectContext, Diagnostic, ScanResult), rule catalog registry, and config loading.
  • src/stackvet/analyzers/: Subsystem analyzers (dependencies, environment, imports, packaging). Analyzers inspect ProjectContext and yield structured Diagnostic objects.
  • src/stackvet/remediation/: Safe, deterministic fix generation and diff planning engine.
  • src/stackvet/reporters/: Terminal, JSON, SARIF, HTML report generator, and GitHub Actions PR annotator.
  • src/stackvet/tui/: Interactive Rich-based terminal dashboard (stackvet inspect / stackvet ui).
  • src/stackvet/visualizers/: Dependency and circular import tree visualizers (stackvet graph).

docs.title: 4. Adding a New Diagnostic Rule
docs.text:
Adding new rules is straightforward and modular:

  1. Assign a Stable Rule ID:
  2. DEP-xxx: Dependency constraint, missing requirement, or version drift.
  3. ENV-xxx: Python interpreter, Docker runtime, or CI matrix drift.
  4. IMP-xxx: Circular imports or broken module import paths.

  5. PKG-xxx: PEP 621 packaging and metadata validation.

  6. Register in Rules Registry:

  7. Add rule metadata (title, severity, documentation, description) in src/stackvet/rules/registry.py.

  8. Implement Analyzer Check:

  9. Add the logic to the appropriate analyzer in src/stackvet/analyzers/.

  10. Ensure the diagnostic includes clear evidence (facts and file sources) and actionable suggestions (recommended CLI command or code snippet).

  11. Add Automated Remediation (Optional):

  12. If the issue can be safely and deterministically resolved, implement a fix handler in src/stackvet/remediation/engine.py.

  13. Write Comprehensive Unit Tests:

  14. Add positive detection tests and negative (false-positive prevention) tests under tests/analyzers/.

  15. Update Documentation:

  16. Document the rule, its root cause, and remediation steps in docs/rules.md and README.md.

docs.title: 5. Code Quality Standards
docs.text:
• Strict Type Annotations: All functions, methods, and public interfaces must be fully typed (verified with pyright).
  • Zero-Network Analyzer Core: Standard diagnostic checks must remain 100% offline, local, and fast (sub-second execution).
  • Verifiable Evidence: Every flagged diagnostic must provide specific source lines, version facts, or manifest references in its evidence list.
  • Clean Diffs & Safety: Remediation fixes must preview exact diffs and commands before modifying user projects.
  • Passing Matrix: All Tox environments (py310 through py313, lint, typecheck, docs) must pass with 100% test coverage for newly introduced rules.

docs.title: 6. Submitting a Pull Request
docs.text:
1. Fork the repository and create a feature branch (git checkout -b feat/my-new-rule).
  2. Implement your changes following the standards above.
  3. Verify your work locally: 
    uv run tox
  4. Commit your changes with clear, descriptive commit messages.
  5. Push to your branch and submit a Pull Request on GitHub.

docs.title: Contributing Diagnostic Rules to StackVet
docs.text: StackVet enforces strict standards for all diagnostic rules to ensure deterministic execution, actionable guidance, and zero false positives. Follow this guide when proposing or implementing a new diagnostic rule.

docs.title: 1. Rule ID Taxonomy Standards
docs.text:
Every diagnostic rule must use a standardized 2 to 5 letter uppercase prefix, a hyphen (-), and a 3-digit zero-padded number (e.g., DEP-008, RCT-006):

Prefix Domain / Technology Example Rules DEP- Python dependency declarations & resolution DEP-001, DEP-002 NDEP- Node.js / JavaScript / TypeScript dependencies NDEP-001, NDEP-004 IMP- Python imports & module structure IMP-001, IMP-004 ARC- Architectural layer constraints ARC-001, ARC-002 SEC- Vulnerability & security posture SEC-001, SEC-002 ENV- Runtime & environment drift ENV-001, ENV-003 DISC- Discovery, file parsing & scanner limits DISC-001, DISC-005 CI- CI/CD workflow security & hygiene CI-001, CI-005 DJG- Django framework best practices DJG-001, DJG-006 CEL- Celery task & worker safety CEL-001, CEL-004 FAP- FastAPI API hygiene & async safety FAP-001, FAP-005 SQL- SQLAlchemy session & query optimization SQL-001, SQL-030 RCT- React component & hooks rules RCT-001, RCT-005 NXT- Next.js App Router & server/client safety NXT-001, NXT-002

docs.title: 2. Catalog Registration
docs.text:
All rules must be registered in crates/stackvet-core/src/rules_catalog.rs inside the ALL_RULES array:

RuleMeta {
    id: "DEP-008",
    category: "dependencies",
    title: "Pinned dependency conflicts with runtime platform",
    severity: "ERROR", // HINT, INFO, WARNING, WARN, ERROR, or CRITICAL
    description: "A dependency declaration specifies platform constraints that exclude the current target environment.",
    remediation: "Update the environment markers in pyproject.toml to accommodate the target platforms.",
}

Rules are validated at compile and test time using validate_rule(&rule). Empty fields or non-standard IDs will fail automated verification.

docs.title: 3. Zero False Positives & Paired Fixtures
docs.text:
Every rule implementation must include paired positive and negative regression test fixtures:

  1. Positive Fixture (tests/fixtures/regression/positive/<rule_id>_*.py or appropriate extension):
  2. A minimal reproducer demonstrating the exact defect triggering the rule.
  3. Negative Fixture (tests/fixtures/regression/negative/<rule_id>_*.py or appropriate extension):
  4. A idiomatic, valid code pattern that must never trigger the diagnostic.

These fixtures are continuously executed by tests/diagnostic_accuracy_test.rs.

docs.title: 4. AST-First Parsing (No RegEx for Code Semantics)
docs.text: StackVet strictly prohibits using regular expressions to parse code logic or import statements: - Use ruff_python_parser and ruff_python_ast for Python AST traversal. - Use oxc_parser and oxc_ast for JavaScript/TypeScript AST traversal. - Python package names must always be normalized according to PEP 503 (name.replace('_', '-').to_lowercase()).

docs.title: 5. Standalone & Summary Documentation
docs.text:
Every rule requires two documentation touchpoints:

  1. Individual Rule Document (docs/rules/<RULE_ID>.md): 

    # <RULE_ID>: <Title>

| Attribute | Value |
|-----------|-------|
| **Rule ID** | `<RULE_ID>` |
| **Category** | `<category>` |
| **Default Severity** | `<SEVERITY>` |

## Description
<Detailed explanation of the issue.>

## Why This Matters
<Impact on production stability, performance, security, or maintainability.>

## Remediation
<Step-by-step instructions and code snippets showing how to fix.>

## Configuration & Suppression
<Inline comment suppression syntax and .stackvet.toml override examples.>

  2. Summary Catalog (docs/rules.md): Add the rule under its category section with ID, severity, description, and remediation.

docs.title: 6. Pre-Submission Verification
docs.text:
Run the rule audit script and test suite before submitting a Pull Request:

# Automated rule catalog & documentation audit
node scripts/audit_rules.js

# Rust catalog integrity & documentation test
cargo test -p stackvet-core --test rule_audit_test

# Full suite verification
cargo fmt --all --check
cargo clippy --all-targets --all-features
cargo test --all-targets --all-features

docs.title: StackVet Machine-Readable Diagnostics Schema
docs.text: This document defines the stable diagnostic schema and source location conventions used by StackVet for CI/CD integrations, GitHub Code Scanning, and IDE tooling.

docs.title: 1. Schema Versioning & Compatibility
docs.text:
StackVet adheres to Semantic Versioning for its diagnostic data interchange format:

Schema Property Current Version Compatibility Guarantee schema_version "1.0.0" Additive, backward-compatible evolutions retain major version 1. Breaking alterations bump major version.

docs.title: Compatibility Rules
docs.text:
• Deserializer Resilience: Consumers must ignore unrecognized keys to permit seamless schema evolution.
  • Backward Compatibility: Reports produced without schema_version, tool, or summary deserialize cleanly using sensible defaults.
  • Explicit Missing Data: When a check evaluates workspace-wide state (such as missing Dockerfile or pyproject.toml), physical file locations are explicitly omitted (normalized_path() == None, SARIF locations: [], table display "-") rather than fabricating line 1 positions.

docs.title: 2. JSON Report Specification (--format json)

docs.title: Summary Object Fields
docs.text:
• total_issues: Total count of active diagnostics reported.
  • critical_count, error_count, warning_count, info_count, hint_count: Issue breakdown by severity.
  • fixable_count: Count of diagnostics offering automated, format-preserving fixes.
  • is_complete (boolean): Always emitted. Indicates whether the scan executed completely across all eligible files. Any DISC-* discovery or resilience diagnostic sets is_complete to false.
  • incomplete_reasons (array of strings, optional): Emitted whenever is_complete is false. Contains human-readable reason strings describing why analysis was incomplete (e.g. malformed manifests, syntax errors, or files exceeding scan size/depth limits).

docs.title: Line and Column Conventions
docs.text:
• 1-based Indexing: All line and column numbers are 1-indexed. The first character on the first line of a file is at (line: 1, col: 1).
  • Unicode Awareness: Column numbers count Unicode characters (scalar values / code points) rather than raw UTF-8 byte offsets. Multi-byte UTF-8 sequences (such as emojis or CJK characters) occupy 1 character column.
  • Cross-Platform Path Normalization: All paths use forward slashes (/) and strip Windows UNC prefixes (\\?\).
  • Multiline Statement Spans: For imports or expressions spanning multiple lines, start_line and start_col mark the beginning of the statement or alias, while end_line and end_col mark its terminus.

docs.title: 4. SARIF v2.1.0 Format (--format sarif)
docs.text:
StackVet generates OASIS SARIF v2.1.0 compatible reports for GitHub Code Scanning and IDE SARIF viewers:

  • Rule Catalog Registration: The runs[0].tool.driver.rules array contains descriptors only for rule IDs present in emitted diagnostics, and is omitted when no results exist. For each emitted rule ID, it includes rule title, description, remediation help, category tags, and default severity level.
  • Physical Locations & Regions: Each result provides physicalLocation.artifactLocation.uri and detailed region bounds (startLine, startColumn, endLine, endColumn, and snippet).
  • Related Locations: Circular import hops, multi-file cycles, or duplicate import sites populate relatedLocations.
  • Automated Fixes: When automated remediation is available, the SARIF fixes array specifies fileChanges and replacements targeting the relevant file and deleted region.
{
  "$schema": "https://raw.githubusercontent.com/oasis-tcs/sarif-spec/master/Schemata/sarif-schema-2.1.0.json",
  "version": "2.1.0",
  "runs": [
    {
      "tool": {
        "driver": {
          "name": "stackvet",

            {
              "id": "DEP-002",
              "name": "Undeclared dependency import",
              "shortDescription": { "text": "Undeclared dependency import" },
              "fullDescription": { "text": "A module imports an external third-party package not declared in the project manifest." },
              "help": { "text": "A module imports an external third-party package not declared in the project manifest.\n\nRemediation: Add the missing package to direct dependencies." },
              "helpUri": "https://github.com/stackvet/stackvet/blob/main/docs/rules/DEP-002.md",
              "defaultConfiguration": { "level": "error" },
              "properties": {
                "category": "dependency",
                "tags": ["dependency"]
              }
            }
          ]
        }
      },
      "results": [
        {
          "ruleId": "DEP-002",
          "level": "error",
          "message": { "text": "Package 'requests' is imported in source code but not declared in pyproject.toml" },
          "locations": [
            {
              "physicalLocation": {
                "artifactLocation": {
                  "uri": "src/api/client.py",
                  "uriBaseId": "%SRCROOT%"
                },
                "region": {
                  "startLine": 10,
                  "startColumn": 5,
                  "endLine": 10,
                  "endColumn": 20,
                  "snippet": { "text": "import requests" }
                }
              }
            }
          ],
          "relatedLocations": [
            {
              "id": 1,
              "physicalLocation": {
                "artifactLocation": {
                  "uri": "tests/test_client.py",
                  "uriBaseId": "%SRCROOT%"
                },

                  "startLine": 4,
                  "startColumn": 1,
                  "endLine": 4,
                  "endColumn": 16
                }
              },
              "message": { "text": "Also imported here" }
            }
          ],
          "fixes": [
            {
              "description": { "text": "Add requests to pyproject.toml" },
              "fileChanges": [
                {
                  "artifactLocation": {
                    "uri": "pyproject.toml",
                    "uriBaseId": "%SRCROOT%"
                  },
                  "replacements": [
                    {

                        "startLine": 15,

                      },

                      }
                    }
                  ]
                }
              ]
            }
          ]
        }
      ]
    }
  ]

docs.title: Getting Started with stackvet
docs.text: stackvet is a high-performance, polyglot diagnostic and project health engine for Python, Node.js/TypeScript, Docker, and CI/CD environments. It analyzes your project configuration, environment, source code imports, ASTs, and dependency trees to pinpoint health issues and suggest safe, actionable fixes.

docs.title: 1. Installation & Execution
docs.text:
Ephemeral Run (npx)Using npm (Node.js)Using pnpmUsing yarnEphemeral Run (uvx / pipx)Using uv (Python)Using pip (Python)Using poetryVia Cargo (Rust)Global CLI ToolFrom GitHub (Latest)From Local Codebase 
# Run project health scorecard without installing
npx @inzamol/stackvet doctor

# Run detailed diagnostic scan
npx @inzamol/stackvet scan

# Run automated remediation
npx @inzamol/stackvet fix

# Install as dev dependency
npm install --save-dev @inzamol/stackvet

# Run health check
npx stackvet doctor

# Install as dev dependency
pnpm add -D @inzamol/stackvet

# Run health check
pnpm exec stackvet doctor

# Install as dev dependency
yarn add -D @inzamol/stackvet

# Run health check
yarn stackvet doctor

# Run project health scorecard

docs.title: 2. Initialize Project Configuration (stackvet init)
docs.text:
Before running extensive scans or configuring custom rule thresholds, initialize standard settings in your pyproject.toml:

stackvet init

This creates a standard [tool.stackvet] configuration block without overwriting any of your existing project settings:

[tool.stackvet]
min_severity = "warning"

[tool.stackvet.dependencies]
ignore = [
    "amqp",
]

[tool.stackvet.rules]
DEP-003 = "warning"
SQL-014 = "error"

[tool.stackvet.paths]
exclude = [
    "tests",
    "migrations",
]

You can also generate a ready-to-run GitHub Actions workflow:

stackvet init --ci github
