docs.title: GitHub Code Scanning Integration
docs.text: StackVet produces fully compliant OASIS SARIF 2.1.0 (Static Analysis Results Interchange Format) reports designed for direct ingestion into GitHub Advanced Security / GitHub Code Scanning.

docs.title: 1. Quick Setup: GitHub Actions Workflow
docs.text:
Create .github/workflows/stackvet-analysis.yml in your repository:

name: "StackVet Security & Health Scan"

on:
  push:
    branches: [ "main" ]
  pull_request:
    branches: [ "main" ]
  schedule:
    - cron: '30 4 * * 1' # Weekly scan every Monday at 04:30 UTC

permissions:
  contents: read
  security-events: write
  actions: read

jobs:
  analyze:
    name: Run StackVet Diagnostics
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest

    steps:
      - name: Checkout repository
        uses: actions/checkout@v4

      - name: Set up Python
        uses: actions/setup-python@v5
        with:
          python-version: "3.11"

      - name: Install StackVet
        run: |
          pip install stackvet
          # Or download binary / use npm: npx -y @inzamol/stackvet

      - name: Run StackVet Scan
        run: |
          stackvet scan --format sarif --output stackvet-results.sarif || true

      - name: Upload SARIF to GitHub Code Scanning
        uses: github/codeql-action/upload-sarif@v3
        with:
          sarif_file: stackvet-results.sarif
          category: stackvet-diagnostics

[!IMPORTANT] The workflow requires security-events: write permissions to upload SARIF results to GitHub Code Scanning. For public repositories, GitHub Code Scanning is free. For private repositories, GitHub Advanced Security is required.

docs.title: 2. SARIF Level Mapping
docs.text:
StackVet diagnostic severities map directly to GitHub Code Scanning alert levels:

StackVet Severity SARIF Level GitHub Alert State Blocks PR Merge (if configured) CRITICAL error Critical / Error Yes ERROR error Error Yes WARNING warning Warning Optional rule INFO note Notice / Info No HINT note Recommendation No

docs.title: 3. Advanced Features Supported in Code Scanning
3.1 Relative URIs and %SRCROOT%
docs.text: StackVet relativizes all repository file paths against %SRCROOT%, URI-encoding spaces and special characters. This ensures GitHub can link findings directly to source code diffs in Pull Requests.

docs.title: 3.2 Precise Multiline Regions & Snippets
docs.text: When diagnostics include line and column spans (startLine, startColumn, endLine, endColumn), GitHub highlights the exact lines and tokens in the file view.

docs.title: 3.3 Related Locations & Dependency Chains
docs.text: For complex diagnostics like circular imports (IMP-001) or architectural layer violations (ARC-001), StackVet populates relatedLocations. GitHub Code Scanning displays the step-by-step navigation path through the cycle directly in the alert details.

docs.title: 3.4 Automated Fixes in PR Diffs
docs.text: When StackVet provides automated remediations (e.g., updating version pins in pyproject.toml), fix changes are embedded in the SARIF fixes array.

docs.title: 4. Local Validation
docs.text:
To validate your generated SARIF file locally prior to pushing:

# Generate SARIF report
stackvet scan --format sarif --output scan.sarif

# Verify SARIF format
node -e "
  const sarif = JSON.parse(require('fs').readFileSync('scan.sarif', 'utf8'));
  console.log('Version:', sarif.version);
  console.log('Total Results:', sarif.runs[0].results.length);
"

docs.title: Self-Contained HTML Report
docs.text: stackvet can generate a single-file, zero-dependency, self-contained HTML report that is fully portable and interactive. You can open it in any web browser, attach it to CI artifacts, or email it to teammates.

docs.title: 1. Generating an HTML Report
docs.text:
Use the --html flag with stackvet scan:

# Generate report for current project
stackvet scan --html report.html

# Scan a microservice and write to a specific location
stackvet scan ./services/auth --html ./build/auth-health.html

# Combine with strict mode
stackvet scan --strict --html health-report.html

docs.title: 2.1 Zero External Dependencies
docs.text:
• All styles (CSS) and interactive scripts (vanilla JavaScript) are embedded directly in a single .html file.
  • Works 100% offline — no CDNs, external web fonts, or tracking scripts required.

docs.title: 2.2 Interactive Circular Health Score
docs.text:
• Displays the project's health score (0–100) using a smooth SVG circular progress gauge.
  • Dynamically color-coded: Green (80–100), Yellow (50–79), Red (0–49).

docs.title: 2.3 Real-Time Search & Filtering
docs.text:
• Search Bar: Instant client-side filtering by rule ID (DEP-002), title, description, or file name.
  • Severity Filters: Filter diagnostics by All, Errors Only, or Warnings Only with interactive counters.

docs.title: 2.4 Detailed Diagnostic Cards
docs.text: Each finding card includes: - Severity pill badge and rule ID tag. - Location badge (e.g., pyproject.toml, main.py:14). - Collapsible Evidence section listing facts extracted from manifests and AST. - Remediation Box with one-click copy buttons for CLI commands and code snippets.

docs.title: 2.5 Dark / Light Mode Toggle
docs.text:
• Includes a theme switch button in the top navigation bar.
  • Automatically detects the user's system preferences (prefers-color-scheme).

docs.title: 3. Automating in GitHub Actions
docs.text:
You can automatically generate and upload the HTML report as a build artifact on every Pull Request:

name: Project Health Scan

on: [push, pull_request]

jobs:
  health-check:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      - uses: astral-sh/setup-uv@v5

      - name: Generate HTML Report
        run: uv run stackvet scan --html stackvet-report.html
        if: always()

      - name: Upload Report Artifact
        uses: actions/upload-artifact@v4
        with:
          name: stackvet-health-report
          path: stackvet-report.html
        if: always()

docs.title: Pre-commit Hook Integration
docs.text: Catch dependency drift, missing imports, and circular cycles before code is ever committed with stackvet's native pre-commit integration.

docs.title: 1. Quick Setup
docs.text:
Add the following to your project's .pre-commit-config.yaml:

repos:
  - repo: https://github.com/inzamol/stackvet
    rev: v0.1.0
    hooks:
      # 1. Diagnostic scan (blocking on warnings & errors)
      - id: stackvet-scan
        args: [--strict, --offline]

      # 2. Optional: Auto-fix safe issues on commit
      # - id: stackvet-fix

Install and activate the hooks in your local Git repository:

pre-commit install

docs.title: 2.1 stackvet-scan
docs.text:
Runs stackvet scan across your repository.

  • Default Arguments: [--strict, --offline]
  • Behavior: Fast, airgapped execution. Fails the commit if any blocking errors or warnings are detected.

docs.title: 2.2 stackvet-fix
docs.text:
Runs stackvet fix -y across your repository.

  • Default Arguments: [-y, --offline]
  • Behavior: Automatically remediates safe issues (like adding missing dependencies to pyproject.toml) and stages the clean file.

docs.title: 3. Testing Hooks Locally
docs.text:
Run pre-commit against all files without committing:

pre-commit run --all-files

docs.title: Publishing Guide: npm & PyPI
docs.text: This guide walks you through publishing StackVet to both the npm Registry (for Node.js / JavaScript users) and PyPI (for Python users).

docs.title: Table of Contents
docs.text:
1. Version Synchronization
  2. Publishing to npm
  3. Prerequisites
  4. Automated Publishing via GitHub Actions (Recommended)
  5. Manual Publishing via CLI
  6. Verifying npm Installation
  7. Publishing to PyPI
  8. Prerequisites
  9. Automated Publishing via GitHub Actions (Recommended)
  10. Manual Publishing via CLI
  11. Verifying PyPI Installation
  12. Troubleshooting & FAQs

docs.title: 1. Version Synchronization
docs.text:
Before releasing a new version, ensure the version number is synchronized across the project manifests:

  1. crates/stackvet-cli/Cargo.toml: version = "0.1.0"
  2. packages/npm/package.json: "version": "0.1.0"
  3. pyproject.toml: version = "0.1.0"

Commit your version updates: 

git add .
git commit -m "chore: bump version to 0.1.0"

docs.title: 2. Publishing to npm
docs.text: StackVet's npm distribution is located in packages/npm/ and ships a cross-platform executable runner (bin/stackvet.js) bundled with the native Rust binary.

docs.title: A. Prerequisites (npm)
docs.text:
1. An active account at npmjs.com.
  2. Enable Two-Factor Authentication (2FA).
  3. Generate an Automation Token:
  4. Go to npmjs.com -> Click your Profile -> Access Tokens.
  5. Click Generate New Token -> Choose Classic Token -> Select Automation.
  6. Copy the generated token (starts with npm_...).

docs.title: B. Automated Publishing via GitHub Actions
docs.text: The repository includes a ready-to-run workflow at .github/workflows/publish-npm.yml.

docs.title: Step 1: Configure GitHub Secret
docs.text:
1. Open your repository on GitHub.
  2. Go to Settings -> Secrets and variables -> Actions.
  3. Click New repository secret.
  4. Set:
  5. Name: NPM_TOKEN
  6. Secret: Paste your npm automation token.
  7. Click Add secret.

docs.title: Step 2: Trigger Publication
docs.text:
Create and push a Git release tag: 

git tag v0.1.0
git push origin v0.1.0

GitHub Actions will automatically: 1. Compile the optimized native Rust binary. 2. Bundle the binary into the npm package structure. 3. Validate that stackvet --version executes cleanly. 4. Publish stackvet to https://registry.npmjs.org/ with public access.

Tip (Dry Run): You can also manually trigger this workflow via the Actions tab on GitHub and check the dry_run option to test packaging without publishing.

docs.title: C. Manual Publishing via CLI
docs.text:
To build and publish manually from your local machine:

# 1. Build and package the npm distribution
npm run build:npm

# 2. Navigate to the npm package folder
cd packages/npm

# 3. Log into npm (if not already logged in)
npm login

# 4. Publish to registry
npm publish --access public

docs.title: D. Verifying npm Installation
docs.text:
After publishing, test running StackVet directly with npx (no prior installation needed):

# Run instantly via npx
npx stackvet doctor

# Or install globally
npm install -g stackvet
stackvet --version

# Or install as a project devDependency
pnpm add -D stackvet
# or
npm install --save-dev stackvet

docs.title: 3. Publishing to PyPI
docs.text: StackVet uses Maturin (bindings = "bin") to build native Python wheels containing the compiled binary for Linux, macOS, and Windows.

docs.title: A. Prerequisites (PyPI)
docs.text:
1. An active account at pypi.org.
  2. Enable 2FA on PyPI.

docs.title: B. Automated Publishing via GitHub Actions (PyPI)
docs.text:
The repository includes a multi-platform build workflow at .github/workflows/publish-pypi.yml.

It uses PyPI's modern Trusted Publishing (OIDC), eliminating the need to store long-lived API tokens.

docs.title: Setting up PyPI Trusted Publishing (Zero-Token OIDC)
docs.text:
1. Log in to pypi.org and go to Account Settings -> Publishing.
  2. Click Add a new pending publisher.
  3. Enter:
  4. PyPI Project Name: stackvet
  5. Owner: Your GitHub username or organization (e.g. inzamol)
  6. Repository name: stackvet
  7. Workflow name: publish-pypi.yml
  8. Environment name: pypi
  9. Click Add.

docs.title: Triggering Publication
docs.text:
Push your version tag: 

git tag v0.1.0
git push origin v0.1.0

GitHub Actions will automatically: 1. Matrix build wheels for: - Linux: x86_64 and aarch64 - Windows: x86_64 - macOS: x86_64 and aarch64 (Apple Silicon) 2. Build the source distribution (sdist). 3. Securely upload all artifacts to PyPI via OIDC.

Alternative (API Token): If you prefer an API token, create a token on PyPI and add it to GitHub Secrets as PYPI_API_TOKEN.

docs.title: C. Manual Publishing via CLI (PyPI)
docs.text:
To manually build and upload the current platform's wheel and sdist:

# 1. Install maturin and twine
pip install maturin twine

# 2. Build the wheel and source distribution
npm run build:pypi
# Artifacts are written to dist/pypi/

# 3. Verify packages
twine check dist/pypi/*

# 4. Upload to PyPI
twine upload dist/pypi/*

docs.title: D. Verifying PyPI Installation
docs.text:
Test running StackVet via Python tooling:

# Run instantly with uvx (no install required)
uvx stackvet doctor

# Or install with pip / pipx
pip install stackvet
# or
pipx install stackvet

stackvet --version

docs.title: Q: npm ERR! 403 Forbidden - You do not have permission to publish "stackvet"
docs.text:
• The package name stackvet may already be registered or reserved by someone else on npm.
  • If the name is taken, you can publish under an npm organization scope (e.g. @yourorg/stackvet) by updating "name": "@yourorg/stackvet" in packages/npm/package.json.

docs.title: Q: HTTPError: 400 Bad Request from PyPI - File already exists
docs.text: • PyPI never allows re-uploading an existing version number. If a build failed or needs changes, increment the patch version (e.g. 0.1.1) in pyproject.toml and Cargo.toml.

docs.title: Q: Windows error: os error 32 (file in use) during local cargo build
docs.text:
• This occurs if Windows Defender or a file indexer holds a temporary .rcgu.o lock on the build directory.
  • StackVet is configured with .cargo/config.toml targeting ~/.cargo-target/stackvet outside watched directories to eliminate lock collisions.

docs.title: Safe Automated Remediation
docs.text:
stackvet follows a strict design principle: Diagnose first. Explain second. Fix safely.

Unlike aggressive tools that rewrite code unpredictably, stackvet fix computes deterministic, reversible remediation plans. You can preview proposed diffs in advance with --dry-run, apply fixes interactively, or automate safe repairs in CI scripts.

docs.title: 1. Basic Usage
docs.text:
# Preview proposed unified color diffs without modifying files
stackvet fix --diff

# Interactive confirmation prompt before applying each individual fix
stackvet fix -i
# or
stackvet fix --interactive

# Preview proposed plan in tabular dry-run mode
stackvet fix --dry-run

# Automatically apply all safe fixes without prompting
stackvet fix -y

# Fix only a specific rule (e.g. missing dependencies)
stackvet fix --rule DEP-002 -y

# Apply fixes and execute package manager sync commands
stackvet fix --sync -y

docs.title: 2. Unified Diff Preview Mode (--diff)
docs.text:
Before modifying any files on disk, inspect the exact line-by-line changes stackvet fix proposes using --diff:

stackvet fix --diff

--- pyproject.toml
+++ pyproject.toml
@@ -8,6 +8,7 @@
 dependencies = [
     "click>=8.0.0",
     "rich>=13.0.0",
+    "httpx>=0.27.0",
 ]

docs.title: 3. Interactive Remediation (-i / --interactive)
docs.text:
Run fixes in interactive step-through mode where each individual diagnostic fix prompts for your explicit approval before mutating configuration or source code:

stackvet fix -i

[1/2] Apply fix for DEP-002 (Add 'httpx' to pyproject.toml)? [y/N]: y
  + Successfully applied fix to pyproject.toml

[2/2] Apply fix for PKG-001 (Initialize pyproject.toml metadata)? [y/N]: n
  - Skipped fix for PKG-001

docs.title: 4. Safety Guarantees & Remediation Levels
docs.text:
stackvet classifies fixes into four safety categories:

Fix Category Example Behavior Safe (Deterministic) Adding missing dependencies to pyproject.toml (DEP-002)Adding default [project] / [tool.stackvet] settings (PKG-001) Applied automatically with -y or after interactive confirmation. Review Required Removing unimported declared dependencies (DEP-003) Requires explicit review because packages may be used dynamically, as plugins, or as database drivers. Skipped during -y. Command-Assisted Running uv add or pip install (DEP-001, DEP-005, DEP-006) Proposed as shell commands. Only executed if --sync is explicitly passed. Manual / Complex Refactoring circular import cycles (IMP-001) Provides architectural refactoring hints and code snippets for human review; no blind mutations.

docs.title: 5. Remediation Plan Inspection (Dry Run)
docs.text:
Running stackvet fix --dry-run displays available automated fixes and diff previews:

Found 2 automated fix(es):
1. pyproject.toml -> Add 'httpx' to project dependencies
2. pyproject.toml -> Remove unused dependency 'requests'

--- Proposed Changes (Preview) ---

File: pyproject.toml
@@ -10,3 +10,4 @@
 [project]
 dependencies = [
+    "httpx",
-    "requests",
 ]

Dry-run complete. No files were modified.

docs.title: 6. Package Manager Auto-Sync
docs.text:
When dependencies are modified, running stackvet fix --sync automatically calls the detected package manager (uv sync, poetry install, pip install) to keep your active virtual environment in lockstep:

stackvet fix --sync -y

docs.title: Diagnostic Rules Catalog
docs.text: stackvet rule IDs are stable public identifiers. This catalog lists all supported diagnostic checks, their default severities, and remediation strategies.

docs.title: 1.1 DEP-001: Dependency Constraint Conflict
docs.text:
• Default Severity: ERROR
  • Description: Two or more declared or transitive dependencies have incompatible version constraints.
  • Remediation: Upgrade the conflicting package or loosen the version pin to satisfy all requirements.

docs.title: 1.2 DEP-002: Missing Dependency Declaration
docs.text:
• Default Severity: ERROR
  • Description: A third-party package is imported in source code but is not declared in project dependencies.
  • Remediation: Add the missing package to your pyproject.toml or requirements.txt.

docs.title: 1.3 DEP-003: No Direct Import Detected
docs.text:
• Default Severity: WARNING
  • Description: A package is declared as a direct dependency, but no direct imports were detected across project source files. This detects the absence of a detected direct import, not proof that the dependency is unused. Dependencies may still be required at runtime through plugins, configuration, framework integration, CLI entrypoints, or indirect mechanisms.
  • Remediation: Verify if this dependency is used dynamically, required as a plugin/driver/runtime configuration, or can be safely removed.

docs.title: 1.4 DEP-004: Python Compatibility Mismatch
docs.text:
• Default Severity: WARNING
  • Description: A package requires a Python version incompatible with the target project runtime.
  • Remediation: Update your target Python version or install a version of the package compatible with your Python runtime.

docs.title: 1.5 DEP-005: Installed/Declaration Mismatch
docs.text:
• Default Severity: WARNING
  • Description: The package version installed in the virtualenv does not match the pinned requirement in project declaration.
  • Remediation: Sync your virtual environment using your package manager (e.g. uv sync or poetry install).

docs.title: 1.6 DEP-006: Vulnerable Transitive Dependency
docs.text:
• Default Severity: ERROR
  • Description: A security vulnerability has been identified in a direct or transitive dependency.
  • Remediation: Update the vulnerable dependency or apply vendor security patches.

docs.title: 1.7 DEP-007: Undeclared Transitive Dependency
docs.text:
• Default Severity: WARNING
  • Description: A package is imported in source code and provided transitively by a dependency, but is not declared directly in project dependencies.
  • Remediation: Add the transitive dependency directly to your pyproject.toml or requirements.txt.

docs.title: 2.1 SEC-001: Security Analysis Unavailable
docs.text:
• Default Severity: WARNING
  • Description: The advisory database (OSV.dev) could not be reached to perform vulnerability checks.
  • Remediation: Check your internet connection or run with --offline to skip security checks.

docs.title: 2.2 SEC-002: Stale Vulnerability Advisory Database Cache
docs.text:
• Default Severity: WARNING
  • Description: Vulnerability analysis was performed using a local cache that has exceeded its configured time-to-live (TTL).
  • Remediation: Run with '--refresh-vuln-cache' or verify internet access to update the local advisory database.

docs.title: 3.1 ENV-001: Python Version Drift
docs.text:
• Default Severity: WARNING
  • Description: The active Python interpreter version differs from the project's target runtime specification.
  • Remediation: Ensure the virtual environment is built using the configured target Python version.

docs.title: 3.2 ENV-002: Docker Runtime Drift
docs.text:
• Default Severity: WARNING
  • Description: The Python version in Dockerfile/docker-compose differs from the project's target runtime.
  • Remediation: Update the base image tag in your Dockerfile to match your project's target Python version.

docs.title: 3.3 ENV-003: CI Runtime Drift
docs.text:
• Default Severity: WARNING
  • Description: CI workflow test matrix does not cover or differs from declared project Python versions.
  • Remediation: Align your CI matrix with the Python versions specified in pyproject.toml.

docs.title: 4.1 IMP-001: Circular Import Detected
docs.text:
• Default Severity: ERROR
  • Description: An import cycle exists between two or more modules, which may cause runtime initialization errors.
  • Remediation: Refactor shared dependencies into a separate module or use deferred/lazy imports.

docs.title: 4.2 IMP-002: Unresolved Local Import
docs.text:
• Default Severity: ERROR
  • Description: A local module imported in source code could not be resolved on the project's Python path.
  • Remediation: Verify the module name and ensure source directory is marked on the PYTHONPATH or package root.

docs.title: 4.3 IMP-003: Unused / Orphan Local Module
docs.text:
• Default Severity: WARNING
  • Description: A Python source file exists in the project but is never imported or referenced by any other module, entry point, or test file.
  • Remediation: Review if this module is obsolete and can be safely deleted or integrated into your package exports.

docs.title: 4.4 IMP-004: Deprecated or Removed Standard Library Module
docs.text:
• Default Severity: ERROR
  • Description: A standard library module imported in source code was deprecated or completely removed in modern Python (PEP 594).
  • Remediation: Replace the removed stdlib module with its modern replacement (e.g. importlib instead of imp, subprocess instead of pipes).

docs.title: 4.5 ARC-001: Architecture Layer Violation
docs.text:
• Default Severity: WARNING
  • Description: A module in an upper architectural layer directly imports a lower layer bypassing intermediate abstraction layers (e.g. API importing Database directly instead of through Services/Repositories), or a lower layer imports an upper layer.
  • Remediation: Route access through the designated intermediate service/repository layer or invert the dependency using interfaces/events.

docs.title: 4.6 ARC-002: Architectural Circular Component Dependency
docs.text:
• Default Severity: ERROR
  • Description: A circular dependency cycle exists between high-level architectural components or layers (e.g. Services → Utils → Services).
  • Remediation: Decouple the architectural components by extracting shared utilities, introducing an abstraction layer, or using dependency injection.

docs.title: 5.1 PKG-001: Missing Package Metadata
docs.text:
• Default Severity: WARNING
  • Description: Essential packaging metadata (such as project name, version, or description) is missing.
  • Remediation: Provide project name and version in pyproject.toml [project] table.

docs.title: 5.2 PKG-002: Invalid Project Configuration
docs.text:
• Default Severity: ERROR
  • Description: The project configuration file contains syntax errors or invalid keys.
  • Remediation: Fix configuration syntax to conform to PEP 621 / tool specifications.

docs.title: 6.1 FAP-001: Blocking Call or CPU-Bound Operation in Async Endpoint
docs.text:
• Default Severity: ERROR
  • Description: Synchronous blocking operations (e.g. time.sleep, requests, subprocess, synchronous DB queries) or CPU-bound hashing called inside an async def FastAPI route handler block the asyncio event loop.
  • Remediation: Use non-blocking async alternatives (e.g. asyncio.sleep, httpx.AsyncClient) or run blocking/CPU calls in worker threads via anyio.to_thread.run_sync or fastapi.concurrency.run_in_threadpool.

docs.title: 6.2 FAP-002: Blocking Dependency in Async Path
docs.text:
• Default Severity: WARNING
  • Description: An async route handler depends on a dependency (via Depends) that executes blocking synchronous I/O or CPU operations.
  • Remediation: Refactor dependency to use async operations or execute in a worker threadpool.

docs.title: 6.3 FAP-003: Missing Response Model or Return Type Annotation
docs.text:
• Default Severity: WARNING
  • Description: FastAPI route endpoint does not declare a response_model argument or return type annotation, disabling schema validation and response serialization.
  • Remediation: Add a return type annotation (-> ResponseModel) or pass response_model to the route decorator.

docs.title: 6.4 FAP-004: Insecure CORS or Debug Configuration
docs.text:
• Default Severity: ERROR
  • Description: CORSMiddleware configured with allow_origins=['*'] and allow_credentials=True, or FastAPI instantiated with debug=True.
  • Remediation: Specify explicit trusted origins in allow_origins when credentials are enabled, and disable debug mode in production.

docs.title: 6.5 FAP-005: Missing HTTP Client Timeout Configuration
docs.text:
• Default Severity: WARNING
  • Description: HTTP client (such as httpx.AsyncClient, httpx.Client, or aiohttp.ClientSession) instantiated without an explicit timeout.
  • Remediation: Configure an explicit timeout (e.g. timeout=10.0) to prevent hanging connections.

docs.title: 6.6 FAP-006: Route Path Parameter Template Mismatch
docs.text:
• Default Severity: ERROR
  • Description: A path parameter defined in the route URL template (e.g. '/users/{user_id}') does not match any parameter in the handler function signature.
  • Remediation: Ensure all {param} placeholders in route URL decorators match parameter names in the endpoint function signature.

docs.title: 6.7 FAP-007: Unsafe Yield Dependency Without Try/Finally
docs.text:
• Default Severity: WARNING
  • Description: A generator dependency using yield does not wrap cleanup code in a try...finally block, causing resource and connection leaks on exceptions.
  • Remediation: Wrap the yield and teardown logic in a try...finally block to guarantee resource cleanup.

docs.title: 6.8 FAP-008: Deprecated @app.on_event Lifecycle Hook
docs.text:
• Default Severity: WARNING
  • Description: Using deprecated @app.on_event('startup' / 'shutdown') handlers instead of modern lifespan context managers.
  • Remediation: Migrate @app.on_event to '@asynccontextmanager async def lifespan(app: FastAPI)' and pass to FastAPI(lifespan=lifespan).

docs.title: 6.9 FAP-009: Untyped or Unvalidated Request Body
docs.text:
• Default Severity: WARNING
  • Description: Route handler accepts a raw 'dict', 'Any', or untyped Body parameter instead of a Pydantic model, bypassing automatic request validation.
  • Remediation: Define a Pydantic BaseModel schema for the request payload to ensure type safety and validation.

docs.title: 6.10 FAP-010: Shadowed or Duplicate Route Endpoint
docs.text:
• Default Severity: ERROR
  • Description: Multiple route handlers are registered with the identical HTTP method and path on the same app/router, causing one to shadow the other.
  • Remediation: Ensure all routes have unique method and path combinations, or combine related logic into a single handler.

docs.title: 6.11 FAP-011: Mutable Default Value in Route Parameter
docs.text:
• Default Severity: WARNING
  • Description: Route handler uses a mutable default argument (e.g. list or dict), which can leak state across concurrent requests.
  • Remediation: Use None as default (e.g. filters: list[str] | None = None) or use Field(default_factory=list).

docs.title: 6.12 FAP-012: Invalid Exception Handler Signature
docs.text:
• Default Severity: ERROR
  • Description: Custom @app.exception_handler function does not take the required (request, exc) parameters, causing runtime crashes.
  • Remediation: Ensure custom exception handlers accept exactly two parameters: '(request: Request, exc: Exception)'.

docs.title: 6.13 FAP-013: Untracked asyncio.create_task in Route Handler
docs.text:
• Default Severity: WARNING
  • Description: Spawning raw asyncio.create_task inside route handlers without background task management can cause lost exceptions and unhandled crashes.
  • Remediation: Use FastAPI's built-in BackgroundTasks ('background_tasks.add_task(...)') for request-scoped background jobs.

docs.title: 6.14 FAP-014: Potential Path Traversal in FileResponse
docs.text:
• Default Severity: WARNING
  • Description: FileResponse initialized directly with an unvalidated path variable from route parameters, risking arbitrary file read vulnerabilities.
  • Remediation: Validate and resolve the file path against a trusted base directory before passing to FileResponse.

docs.title: 6.15 FAP-015: Blocking File I/O in Async Endpoint
docs.text:
• Default Severity: ERROR
  • Description: Using synchronous open() or blocking file read/write operations inside an async def route handler blocks the event loop.
  • Remediation: Use 'aiofiles', 'anyio.Path', or run file I/O in a synchronous def route handler.

docs.title: 6.16 FAP-016: Sensitive Field Exposure in Schema
docs.text:
• Default Severity: ERROR
  • Description: Pydantic model schema exposes sensitive password/secret fields without Field(exclude=True) or response filtering.
  • Remediation: Mark sensitive fields with 'Field(exclude=True)' or create a separate output schema (e.g. UserResponse).

docs.title: 6.17 FAP-017: Non-Standard HTTP Status Code on POST or DELETE
docs.text:
• Default Severity: WARNING
  • Description: Mutation routes (POST/DELETE) return default 200 OK instead of standard REST status codes (201 Created or 204 No Content).
  • Remediation: Specify status_code=status.HTTP_201_CREATED on POST routes or status.HTTP_204_NO_CONTENT on DELETE routes.

docs.title: 6.18 FAP-018: Global In-Memory State Mutation in Route Handler
docs.text:
• Default Severity: ERROR
  • Description: Route handler mutates global/module-level collections or variables without synchronization locks, causing concurrency bugs.
  • Remediation: Use a proper database, Redis cache, or an asyncio.Lock for shared state.

docs.title: 6.19 FAP-019: Insecure Cookie Configuration
docs.text:
• Default Severity: ERROR
  • Description: response.set_cookie() called without httponly=True or secure=True flags, exposing cookies to XSS or network interception.
  • Remediation: Set 'httponly=True' and 'secure=True' when storing sensitive session or auth cookies.

docs.title: 6.20 FAP-020: Potential Open Redirect in RedirectResponse
docs.text:
• Default Severity: WARNING
  • Description: RedirectResponse initialized directly with user-supplied URL parameter without domain whitelist validation.
  • Remediation: Validate that the redirect target is a relative path or matches an allowed domain whitelist.

docs.title: 6.21 FAP-021: Router Included Without Tags or Prefix
docs.text:
• Default Severity: WARNING
  • Description: app.include_router() called without 'tags' or 'prefix', leading to unorganized OpenAPI documentation and URL clashes.
  • Remediation: Provide 'prefix' and 'tags' when including routers (e.g. app.include_router(user_router, prefix='/users', tags=['Users'])).

docs.title: 6.22 FAP-022: WebSocket Route Missing Await websocket.accept()
docs.text:
• Default Severity: ERROR
  • Description: WebSocket endpoint sends or receives data before calling 'await websocket.accept()', which causes runtime errors.
  • Remediation: Call 'await websocket.accept()' before reading or writing data to the WebSocket.

docs.title: 6.23 FAP-023: Deprecated Pydantic v1 Config Class
docs.text:
• Default Severity: WARNING
  • Description: Pydantic schema uses deprecated inner 'class Config:' instead of Pydantic v2 'model_config = ConfigDict(...)'.
  • Remediation: Migrate inner 'class Config:' to 'model_config = ConfigDict(...)'.

docs.title: 6.24 FAP-024: Redundant Duplicate Dependency Declaration
docs.text:
• Default Severity: WARNING
  • Description: Route handler declares multiple parameters resolving the exact same dependency callable.
  • Remediation: Consolidate duplicate dependencies into a single parameter.

docs.title: 6.25 FAP-025: Returned HTTPException Instance Instead of Raise
docs.text:
• Default Severity: ERROR
  • Description: Returning an HTTPException instance in a route handler returns a 200 OK HTTP response with the serialized exception object instead of raising an error.
  • Remediation: Use 'raise HTTPException(...)' instead of 'return HTTPException(...)'.

docs.title: 6.26 FAP-026: Deprecated Pydantic v1 @validator or @root_validator
docs.text:
• Default Severity: WARNING
  • Description: Using deprecated Pydantic v1 '@validator' or '@root_validator' decorators instead of Pydantic v2 '@field_validator' or '@model_validator'.
  • Remediation: Migrate to '@field_validator' or '@model_validator' from pydantic.

docs.title: 6.27 FAP-027: Dependency Parameter Missing Type Annotation
docs.text:
• Default Severity: WARNING
  • Description: Route parameter initialized with 'Depends(...)', 'Query(...)', or 'Path(...)' does not specify a type annotation, disabling FastAPI schema generation and static type checking.
  • Remediation: Add explicit type annotation: 'param: Type = Depends(...)' or 'param: Annotated[Type, Depends(...)]'.

docs.title: 6.28 FAP-028: Raw json.loads Called on Request Body
docs.text:
• Default Severity: WARNING
  • Description: Calling 'json.loads(await request.body())' or 'json.loads(request.body)' is an anti-pattern; FastAPI and Starlette provide an optimized built-in 'await request.json()' method.
  • Remediation: Replace 'json.loads(await request.body())' with 'await request.json()'.

docs.title: 6.29 FAP-029: StreamingResponse Initialized Without media_type
docs.text:
• Default Severity: WARNING
  • Description: Instantiating StreamingResponse without specifying 'media_type' can cause clients to misinterpret the streamed content format.
  • Remediation: Pass an explicit media_type argument (e.g. StreamingResponse(stream, media_type='application/json')).

docs.title: 6.30 FAP-030: Missing Route Summary or Docstring for OpenAPI Documentation
docs.text:
• Default Severity: WARNING
  • Description: Public route endpoint does not provide a docstring, 'summary', or 'description', resulting in sparse and incomplete OpenAPI documentation.
  • Remediation: Add a function docstring or pass 'summary=...' in the route decorator.

docs.title: 6.31 FAP-031: Prefer typing.Annotated Over Parameter Default Assignment
docs.text:
• Default Severity: INFO
  • Description: FastAPI strongly recommends using standard typing.Annotated[Type, Depends(...)] instead of parameter default values for cleaner typing and reusable dependencies.
  • Remediation: Refactor parameter to 'param: Annotated[Type, Depends(...)]' or 'param: Annotated[Type, Query(...)]'.

docs.title: 6.32 FAP-032: Redundant jsonable_encoder with response_model
docs.text:
• Default Severity: WARNING
  • Description: Calling jsonable_encoder() inside a route handler that already declares response_model causes double serialization, reducing throughput.
  • Remediation: Return raw objects or dicts directly and let FastAPI's response_model handle serialization.

docs.title: 6.33 FAP-033: Missing from_attributes=True in ORM Response Schema
docs.text:
• Default Severity: WARNING
  • Description: Pydantic response model for ORM/database objects is missing 'model_config = ConfigDict(from_attributes=True)', causing validation failures when serializing ORM instances.
  • Remediation: Add 'model_config = ConfigDict(from_attributes=True)' to the Pydantic schema.

docs.title: 6.34 FAP-034: Missing Await on request.json() or request.body()
docs.text:
• Default Severity: ERROR
  • Description: Calling request.json() or request.body() without 'await' inside an async def route handler assigns an un-awaited coroutine instead of parsed data.
  • Remediation: Add 'await' before 'request.json()' or 'request.body()'.

docs.title: 6.35 FAP-035: Raw Exception Raised Instead of HTTPException
docs.text:
• Default Severity: WARNING
  • Description: Raising generic Exception, ValueError, or RuntimeError in route handlers triggers uncaught 500 Internal Server Errors instead of structured REST HTTP error responses.
  • Remediation: Raise 'HTTPException(status_code=..., detail=...)' for predictable API client error responses.

docs.title: 6.36 FAP-036: Mutating app.state Inside Route Handler
docs.text:
• Default Severity: WARNING
  • Description: Mutating request.app.state or app.state inside per-request route handlers introduces concurrency race conditions. Application state should be initialized in lifespan context managers.
  • Remediation: Initialize shared state in the lifespan context manager before startup rather than modifying app.state in route handlers.

docs.title: 6.37 FAP-037: SecurityScopes Declared with Depends Instead of Security
docs.text:
• Default Severity: WARNING
  • Description: SecurityScopes parameter declared in a dependency using Depends(...) will not receive requested scopes. Use Security(dependency, scopes=[...]) instead.
  • Remediation: Use 'Security(dependency, scopes=[...])' when protecting endpoints with OAuth2 SecurityScopes.

docs.title: 6.38 FAP-038: Hardcoded HTTP Status Code Integer
docs.text:
• Default Severity: INFO
  • Description: Using integer literals for status_code (e.g. status_code=201) reduces readability compared to named constants like status.HTTP_201_CREATED.
  • Remediation: Import status from fastapi (or HTTPStatus from http) and use named constants (e.g. status.HTTP_201_CREATED).

docs.title: 7.1 SQL-001: Potential N+1 Database Query in Loop
docs.text:
• Default Severity: WARNING
  • Description: Executing database queries (session.execute, session.query, session.get, or select()) inside for/while loops causes N+1 performance degradation.
  • Remediation: Batch query objects using 'select(...).where(Model.id.in_(ids))' or eager relationship options (e.g. joinedload/selectinload).

docs.title: 7.2 SQL-002: Session Instantiated Without Context Manager or Cleanup
docs.text:
• Default Severity: WARNING
  • Description: Instantiating a Session without a with-statement context manager or try...finally session.close() causes database connection pool exhaustion.
  • Remediation: Use 'with SessionLocal() as session:' or wrap session lifecycle in a context manager / dependency yield.

docs.title: 7.3 SQL-003: Synchronous DB Operation in Async Event Loop
docs.text:
• Default Severity: ERROR
  • Description: Invoking synchronous database engine calls or synchronous session operations inside an async def function blocks the asyncio event loop.
  • Remediation: Use SQLAlchemy async extension ('create_async_engine' and 'AsyncSession') with async drivers (e.g. asyncpg, aiosqlite).

docs.title: 7.4 SQL-004: Raw SQL String Interpolation (SQL Injection Risk)
docs.text:
• Default Severity: ERROR
  • Description: Constructing SQL queries using f-strings or string formatting with text() or cursor.execute() introduces severe SQL injection vulnerabilities.
  • Remediation: Use bound query parameters with text('SELECT ... WHERE id = :id'), {'id': user_val}.

docs.title: 7.5 SQL-005: Legacy SQLAlchemy 1.x session.query() Syntax
docs.text:
• Default Severity: WARNING
  • Description: Using legacy session.query(...) instead of modern SQLAlchemy 2.0 select() and session.scalars().
  • Remediation: Migrate from 'session.query(User).filter(...)' to 'session.scalars(select(User).where(...))'.

docs.title: 7.6 SQL-006: Missing Relationship Eager Loading Strategy in Async Session
docs.text:
• Default Severity: WARNING
  • Description: Accessing lazy-loaded ORM relationships without explicit joinedload/selectinload in async sessions triggers MissingGreenlet errors.
  • Remediation: Specify 'options(selectinload(Model.relation))' or set lazy='selectin' on relationship definition.

docs.title: 7.7 SQL-007: Uncommitted Transaction in Mutation Function
docs.text:
• Default Severity: WARNING
  • Description: Session performs mutations (session.add / session.delete) but never executes session.commit() or enters a transaction with session.begin().
  • Remediation: Ensure mutations are committed with 'await session.commit()' or executed inside 'with session.begin():'.

docs.title: 7.8 SQL-008: create_engine Missing pool_pre_ping Connection Health Check
docs.text:
• Default Severity: WARNING
  • Description: Creating a database engine without 'pool_pre_ping=True' can lead to runtime disconnect errors when idle connections are closed by firewalls/servers.
  • Remediation: Add 'pool_pre_ping=True' to create_engine() / create_async_engine().

docs.title: 7.9 SQL-009: expire_on_commit=True in AsyncSession
docs.text:
• Default Severity: WARNING
  • Description: Configuring AsyncSession or async_sessionmaker with expire_on_commit=True (the default) causes MissingGreenlet exceptions when accessing committed model attributes.
  • Remediation: Set 'expire_on_commit=False' when instantiating AsyncSession or async_sessionmaker.

docs.title: 7.10 SQL-010: Hardcoded Database Credentials in Connection URL
docs.text:
• Default Severity: ERROR
  • Description: Database URL contains plain-text passwords or secret credentials in source code instead of loading from environment variables.
  • Remediation: Read database connection strings from environment variables (e.g. os.getenv('DATABASE_URL')).

docs.title: 7.11 SQL-011: Unbounded SELECT Query Without LIMIT or Pagination
docs.text:
• Default Severity: WARNING
  • Description: Calling .all() on queries against database tables without limit() or pagination clauses risks memory exhaustion on large datasets.
  • Remediation: Add '.limit(limit)' and pagination parameters to query statements.

docs.title: 7.12 SQL-012: Relationship Cascade Delete Without ForeignKey ondelete CASCADE
docs.text:
• Default Severity: INFO
  • Description: Configuring relationship cascade='all, delete-orphan' without database-level ondelete='CASCADE' on ForeignKey forces slow Python-side row-by-row deletion.
  • Remediation: Add ondelete='CASCADE' to ForeignKey and passive_deletes=True to relationship for database-level cascading.

docs.title: 7.13 SQL-013: Session Flush or Commit Called Inside Loop
docs.text:
• Default Severity: WARNING
  • Description: Calling session.flush() or session.commit() inside loops creates high database roundtrip overhead. Use bulk insert or single commit after loop.
  • Remediation: Move session.commit() outside the loop or use session.execute(insert(Model), batch_data).

docs.title: 7.14 SQL-014: Deprecated declarative_base() Function
docs.text:
• Default Severity: WARNING
  • Description: Using legacy declarative_base() instead of modern SQLAlchemy 2.0 class Base(DeclarativeBase): pass.
  • Remediation: Define 'class Base(DeclarativeBase): pass' from sqlalchemy.orm.

docs.title: 7.15 SQL-015: SQLite Engine Missing check_same_thread=False in Multi-Threaded Application
docs.text:
• Default Severity: WARNING
  • Description: SQLite engine initialized without connect_args={'check_same_thread': False} can cause ProgrammingError in multi-threaded web applications.
  • Remediation: Pass connect_args={'check_same_thread': False} to create_engine() when using SQLite in web applications.

docs.title: 7.16 SQL-016: Missing Database Migration Configuration (Alembic)
docs.text:
• Default Severity: INFO
  • Description: SQLAlchemy database models are defined in the project, but no Alembic migrations directory or alembic.ini configuration exists.
  • Remediation: Initialize database migrations using 'alembic init alembic'.

docs.title: 7.17 SQL-017: Mapped[...] Attribute Missing mapped_column() in 2.0 Declarative Model
docs.text:
• Default Severity: WARNING
  • Description: Using legacy Column() or raw field assignment with Mapped[...] type annotations instead of SQLAlchemy 2.0's native mapped_column().
  • Remediation: Replace 'col: Mapped[int] = Column(Integer)' with 'col: Mapped[int] = mapped_column()'.

docs.title: 7.18 SQL-018: Excessive Connection Pool Size in Single Application Instance
docs.text:
• Default Severity: WARNING
  • Description: create_engine configured with pool_size or max_overflow > 50 in a single instance, risking database connection exhaustion.
  • Remediation: Keep pool_size between 5 and 20 per instance and use external connection poolers (e.g. pgBouncer) for scaling.

docs.title: 7.19 SQL-019: NullPool Configured in Persistent Web Application
docs.text:
• Default Severity: WARNING
  • Description: Using NullPool in persistent web servers disables connection pooling and creates high latency TCP connection overhead on every request.
  • Remediation: Use default QueuePool or AsyncAdaptedQueuePool for persistent web applications; reserve NullPool for AWS Lambda/serverless.

docs.title: 7.20 SQL-020: Declarative ORM Model Missing Primary Key Definition
docs.text:
• Default Severity: ERROR
  • Description: Declarative ORM model defined without at least one primary key column (primary_key=True), which will cause runtime ORM mapping failures.
  • Remediation: Define at least one column with 'primary_key=True' or 'mapped_column(primary_key=True)'.

docs.title: 7.21 SQL-021: Missing session.rollback() in Database Exception Handler
docs.text:
• Default Severity: WARNING
  • Description: Catching exceptions around database queries/mutations without invoking session.rollback() leaves the session in an unusable invalid state.
  • Remediation: Add 'session.rollback()' in exception handlers or use 'with session.begin():' for automatic rollback on error.

docs.title: 7.22 SQL-022: Large Binary or Heavy Text Column Without deferred/load_only Strategy
docs.text:
• Default Severity: INFO
  • Description: Model includes LargeBinary or Large Text column without deferred() loading, causing heavy memory consumption during full-table selects.
  • Remediation: Wrap large blob/text columns with 'deferred(Column(LargeBinary))' or use select(Model).options(load_only(...)).

docs.title: 7.23 SQL-023: ForeignKey Column Defined Without index=True
docs.text:
• Default Severity: WARNING
  • Description: ForeignKey column created without index=True, causing expensive sequential scans during joins, foreign key lookups, and cascade operations.
  • Remediation: Add 'index=True' to ForeignKey column definitions (e.g. Column(Integer, ForeignKey('users.id'), index=True)).

docs.title: 7.24 SQL-024: Insecure Unencrypted Remote Database Connection URL
docs.text:
• Default Severity: WARNING
  • Description: Remote database connection URL targeting external hosts does not specify sslmode=require or ssl=true.
  • Remediation: Append '?sslmode=require' (PostgreSQL) or '?ssl=true' to production database connection strings.

docs.title: 7.25 SQL-025: Deprecated engine.execute() or engine.scalar() Direct Call
docs.text:
• Default Severity: ERROR
  • Description: Calling engine.execute() or engine.scalar() directly is removed in SQLAlchemy 2.0.
  • Remediation: Use explicit connection contexts: 'with engine.connect() as conn: result = conn.execute(stmt)'.

docs.title: 7.26 SQL-026: AsyncSession Instantiated Without Async Context Manager or Await close()
docs.text:
• Default Severity: WARNING
  • Description: AsyncSession created without 'async with' context manager or explicit 'await session.close()', causing connection leaks in async tasks.
  • Remediation: Use 'async with AsyncSessionLocal() as session:' or ensure 'await session.close()' in a finally block.

docs.title: 7.27 SQL-027: Unsafe Concurrent Numeric Balance or Counter Update Without with_for_update()
docs.text:
• Default Severity: WARNING
  • Description: Querying a record and updating numeric counters or balance fields without row-level locking (with_for_update()) causes lost update race conditions.
  • Remediation: Lock rows with 'select(...).with_for_update()' or use atomic SQL increments 'update(Account).values(balance=Account.balance - amt)'.

docs.title: 7.28 SQL-028: Thread-Local scoped_session Used in Async Context
docs.text:
• Default Severity: ERROR
  • Description: Using thread-local scoped_session in async applications causes session sharing across coroutines and race conditions.
  • Remediation: Use async_scoped_session(..., scopefunc=asyncio.current_task) or dependency injection per request.

docs.title: 7.29 SQL-029: Declarative ORM Model Missing tablename Definition
docs.text:
• Default Severity: ERROR
  • Description: Declarative model inheriting from Base/DeclarativeBase does not define tablename or table, causing mapping errors.
  • Remediation: Define 'tablename = "table_name"' on concrete ORM classes (or set 'abstract = True' for mixins).

docs.title: 7.30 SQL-030: Direct DBAPI raw_connection() Used Without Cleanup
docs.text:
• Default Severity: WARNING
  • Description: Calling engine.raw_connection() bypasses connection pool management and leaks connections if not closed explicitly.
  • Remediation: Always close raw DBAPI connections in a try...finally block: 'raw_conn = engine.raw_connection(); try: ... finally: raw_conn.close()'.

docs.title: 8.1 DOC-001: Inefficient Docker Layer Caching
docs.text:
• Default Severity: WARNING
  • Description: Source code is copied before package dependencies are installed (COPY . . before RUN pip install ... or RUN uv sync), invalidating the build cache on every code change.
  • Remediation: Copy dependency manifests (e.g. pyproject.toml, requirements.txt, uv.lock) and install packages before copying the full project directory (COPY . .).

docs.title: 8.2 DOC-002: Root User Container Execution
docs.text:
• Default Severity: WARNING
  • Description: The Dockerfile configures an execution entrypoint (CMD/ENTRYPOINT) without specifying a non-root USER.
  • Remediation: Create and switch to a non-privileged user (e.g. RUN useradd -m -u 1000 appuser && USER appuser) before the container entrypoint.

docs.title: 8.3 DOC-003: Unpinned Base Image Tag
docs.text:
• Default Severity: INFO
  • Description: The base image uses :latest or an unpinned tag, which leads to non-reproducible and unpredictable builds.
  • Remediation: Pin the base image to a specific version or hash (e.g. python:3.12-slim-bookworm).

docs.title: 8.4 DOC-004: Missing .dockerignore File
docs.text:
• Default Severity: WARNING
  • Description: A Dockerfile exists in the project but no .dockerignore file is present, risking baking local virtualenvs, credentials, and temp files into the image.
  • Remediation: Create a .dockerignore file in the repository root excluding .git, .venv, __pycache__, and sensitive files.

docs.title: 8.5 DOC-005: Missing --no-cache-dir in pip install
docs.text:
• Default Severity: INFO
  • Description: pip install inside Dockerfile runs without --no-cache-dir, which unnecessarily bloats the container layer with cached wheels.
  • Remediation: Add --no-cache-dir to pip install commands (e.g. pip install --no-cache-dir -r requirements.txt).

docs.title: 8.6 DOC-006: Sensitive File Copied into Docker Image
docs.text:
• Default Severity: ERROR
  • Description: The Dockerfile explicitly copies sensitive files (.env, private keys, or credentials) into the container image layer.
  • Remediation: Remove sensitive files from COPY instructions and use Docker BuildKit secrets (--mount=type=secret) or runtime environment variables instead.

docs.title: 8.7 DOC-007: Missing HEALTHCHECK Instruction
docs.text:
• Default Severity: INFO
  • Description: The Dockerfile configures a network service or entrypoint without defining a container HEALTHCHECK.
  • Remediation: Add a HEALTHCHECK instruction (e.g. HEALTHCHECK --interval=30s CMD curl -f http://localhost:8000/health || exit 1).

docs.title: 8.8 DOC-008: Missing PYTHONUNBUFFERED Environment Variable
docs.text:
• Default Severity: INFO
  • Description: Python buffers stdout/stderr by default, which delays or prevents real-time container log streaming.
  • Remediation: Add ENV PYTHONUNBUFFERED=1 to your Dockerfile to ensure unbuffered real-time log output.

docs.title: 8.9 DOC-009: Deprecated MAINTAINER Instruction Used
docs.text:
• Default Severity: INFO
  • Description: The MAINTAINER instruction is deprecated in Dockerfile syntax in favor of metadata labels.
  • Remediation: Replace MAINTAINER <author> with LABEL maintainer="<author>".

docs.title: 8.10 DOC-010: Unnecessary sudo Usage in RUN Instruction
docs.text:
• Default Severity: WARNING
  • Description: Commands in Docker RUN instructions execute with root privileges by default, making sudo redundant and error-prone.
  • Remediation: Remove sudo from RUN instructions during image build.

docs.title: 8.11 DOC-011: apt-get install Without Cleanup
docs.text:
• Default Severity: INFO
  • Description: apt-get install inside Dockerfile leaves package lists and recommended dependencies in image layers, bloating image size.
  • Remediation: Use apt-get install -y --no-install-recommends <pkgs> && rm -rf /var/lib/apt/lists/* in the same RUN layer.

docs.title: 8.12 DOC-012: ADD Instruction Used for Local File Copy
docs.text:
• Default Severity: INFO
  • Description: The ADD instruction was used to copy local files where COPY is preferred for predictability and security.
  • Remediation: Replace ADD with COPY unless automatic tar archive extraction or remote URL fetching is explicitly intended.

docs.title: 8.13 DOC-013: Missing PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE
docs.text:
• Default Severity: INFO
  • Description: Python creates .pyc bytecode cache files inside container layers that are usually unnecessary in ephemeral containers.
  • Remediation: Add ENV PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE=1 to prevent writing .pyc files to container filesystem layers.

docs.title: 8.14 DOC-014: Web Server Entrypoint Missing EXPOSE
docs.text:
• Default Severity: INFO
  • Description: The container starts a web server but does not declare the listening network port via EXPOSE.
  • Remediation: Add EXPOSE <port> (e.g. EXPOSE 8000) to document the port on which the container listens.

docs.title: 9.1 ENG-001: Analyzer Execution Failed
docs.text:
• Default Severity: ERROR
  • Description: An analyzer raised an unexpected exception during execution.
  • Remediation: Check the error message or report a bug to the analyzer maintainer.

docs.title: 10.1 DISC-001: Unreadable Source File
docs.text:
• Default Severity: WARNING
  • Description: A source file could not be read during project discovery due to permissions or encoding errors.
  • Remediation: Check file read permissions and ensure file is encoded in valid UTF-8.

docs.title: 10.2 DISC-002: Python Syntax Error in Source File
docs.text:
• Default Severity: WARNING
  • Description: A Python source file contains invalid syntax and could not be parsed into an AST.
  • Remediation: Fix the syntax error in the source file.

docs.title: 10.3 DISC-003: JavaScript or TypeScript Syntax Error in Source File
docs.text:
• Default Severity: WARNING
  • Description: A JavaScript or TypeScript source file contains invalid syntax and could not be parsed into an AST.
  • Remediation: Fix the syntax error in the source file.

docs.title: 10.4 DISC-004: Malformed Project Manifest or Configuration File
docs.text:
• Default Severity: ERROR
  • Description: A project manifest or configuration file contains invalid syntax, corrupted structure, or unreadable content.
  • Remediation: Validate and correct the syntax of the manifest file (e.g. pyproject.toml, package.json, or tsconfig.json).

docs.title: 10.5 DISC-005: Scan Resource Limit or Repository Boundary Exceeded
docs.text:
• Default Severity: WARNING
  • Description: A file, symlink, or directory structure exceeded the configured scanner limits (such as max file size, max depth, or boundary escaping).
  • Remediation: Increase scanner limits in stackvet.toml or exclude the problematic path using .stackvetignore.

docs.title: 11.1 CI-001: CI Python Matrix Version Mismatch
docs.text:
• Default Severity: WARNING
  • Description: CI workflow tests Python versions incompatible with declared project requires-python or classifiers in pyproject.toml.
  • Remediation: Align CI test matrix versions with supported project Python ranges.

docs.title: 11.2 CI-002: Unfrozen Dependency Installation in CI
docs.text:
• Default Severity: WARNING
  • Description: CI workflow installs dependencies without lockfiles or hash verification.
  • Remediation: Use lockfiles (e.g. uv sync --frozen, poetry install --sync, or pip-sync) in CI workflows.

docs.title: 11.3 CI-003: Deprecated or Outdated CI Action Version
docs.text:
• Default Severity: INFO
  • Description: Workflow references a deprecated or end-of-life GitHub Actions version (e.g. actions/checkout@v2, actions/setup-python@v3).
  • Remediation: Upgrade GitHub Actions to current stable major releases (e.g. actions/checkout@v4, actions/setup-python@v5).

docs.title: 11.4 CI-004: Missing Test or Quality Gate in CI Workflow
docs.text:
• Default Severity: INFO
  • Description: Pull request / push workflow contains no test suite, linter, or health checks.
  • Remediation: Add automated test or lint steps (e.g. pytest, ruff, stackvet scan --ci).

docs.title: 11.5 CI-005: Insecure Secret or Token in CI Workflow
docs.text:
• Default Severity: ERROR
  • Description: Potential plaintext secret or token literal detected in workflow file.
  • Remediation: Store credentials in repository secrets (${{ secrets.MY_SECRET }}).

docs.title: 11.6 CI-006: Missing Concurrency Cancellation in PR Workflow
docs.text:
• Default Severity: INFO
  • Description: Pull request workflow lacks concurrency cancellation, causing redundant runner minutes on repeated pushes.
  • Remediation: Add concurrency group with cancel-in-progress: true.

docs.title: 12.1 DJG-001: Insecure Hardcoded DEBUG = True in Django Settings
docs.text:
• Default Severity: ERROR
  • Description: Django settings hardcodes DEBUG = True without environment variable fallback, risking sensitive traceback exposure.
  • Remediation: Load DEBUG dynamically from an environment variable: DEBUG = os.getenv('DJANGO_DEBUG', 'False').lower() == 'true'.

docs.title: 12.2 DJG-002: Hardcoded SECRET_KEY in Django Settings
docs.text:
• Default Severity: ERROR
  • Description: Hardcoded SECRET_KEY literal detected in settings. Secrets must be loaded from environment variables or vault.
  • Remediation: Load SECRET_KEY from environment: SECRET_KEY = os.environ['DJANGO_SECRET_KEY'].

docs.title: 12.3 DJG-003: Insecure Wildcard ALLOWED_HOSTS in Django Settings
docs.text:
• Default Severity: WARNING
  • Description: ALLOWED_HOSTS contains wildcard '*' allowing Host header poisoning in production.
  • Remediation: Explicitly define allowed domain names or load from environment.

docs.title: 12.4 DJG-004: Potential N+1 Database Query in Loop
docs.text:
• Default Severity: WARNING
  • Description: QuerySet execution inside loop causes N+1 query overhead.
  • Remediation: Prefetch related relations before looping: queryset.prefetch_related('...') or select_related('...').

docs.title: 12.5 DJG-005: Django ForeignKey Missing Explicit on_delete
docs.text:
• Default Severity: WARNING
  • Description: models.ForeignKey declared without required on_delete argument.
  • Remediation: Specify explicit on_delete behavior: models.CASCADE, models.PROTECT, or models.SET_NULL.

docs.title: 12.6 DJG-006: Missing CSRF Protection Middleware
docs.text:
• Default Severity: WARNING
  • Description: MIDDLEWARE list is missing 'django.middleware.csrf.CsrfViewMiddleware'.
  • Remediation: Add 'django.middleware.csrf.CsrfViewMiddleware' to MIDDLEWARE.

docs.title: 13.1 CEL-001: Insecure Celery Pickle Serializer Enabled
docs.text:
• Default Severity: ERROR
  • Description: Celery serializer setting uses 'pickle', allowing arbitrary code execution if brokers are compromised.
  • Remediation: Use secure serialization formats like 'json' or 'msgpack'.

docs.title: 13.2 CEL-002: Missing Task Timeout Limits in Celery Task
docs.text:
• Default Severity: WARNING
  • Description: Celery task has no time_limit or soft_time_limit configured.
  • Remediation: Specify time_limit and soft_time_limit on task decorator: @shared_task(time_limit=300, soft_time_limit=240).

docs.title: 13.3 CEL-003: Unbounded Retry Policy on Celery Task
docs.text:
• Default Severity: WARNING
  • Description: Celery task permits unlimited retries, risking broker congestion and infinite retry loops.
  • Remediation: Set explicit max_retries (e.g. max_retries=3, default_retry_delay=60).

docs.title: 13.4 CEL-004: Blocking time.sleep() in Asynchronous Celery Task
docs.text:
• Default Severity: WARNING
  • Description: Async Celery task invokes time.sleep(), blocking the async event loop.
  • Remediation: Use await asyncio.sleep() instead of time.sleep().

docs.title: 14.1 NDEP-001: Missing Node Package
docs.text:
• Default Severity: ERROR
  • Description: Imported package in .ts, .tsx, or .js is missing from package.json dependencies.
  • Remediation: Run pnpm add <pkg> or npm install <pkg>.

docs.title: 14.2 NDEP-002: Unused Node Package
docs.text:
• Default Severity: WARNING
  • Description: Production dependency in package.json is never imported in any source files.
  • Remediation: Remove unused package from dependencies or move to devDependencies.

docs.title: 14.3 NDEP-003: Unmet Peer Dependency
docs.text:
• Default Severity: ERROR
  • Description: Declared package version conflicts with required peer dependency constraints.
  • Remediation: Align installed package versions with peer dependency requirements.

docs.title: 14.4 NDEP-004: Lockfile Out of Sync
docs.text:
• Default Severity: WARNING
  • Description: Package lockfile (pnpm-lock.yaml / package-lock.json) is missing or out of sync.
  • Remediation: Run pnpm install or npm install to generate and sync the lockfile.

docs.title: 14.5 NDEP-005: DevDependency in Production
docs.text:
• Default Severity: ERROR
  • Description: Package from devDependencies is imported inside production source files.
  • Remediation: Move package from devDependencies to dependencies in package.json.

docs.title: 14.6 NDEP-006: Inconsistent Dependency Version
docs.text:
• Default Severity: WARNING
  • Description: Dependency versions across packages, workspace members, or lockfile resolutions are inconsistent or conflicting.
  • Remediation: Align dependency version constraints across packages and synchronize the lockfile.

docs.title: 15.1 RCT-001: Missing Hook Dependencies
docs.text:
• Default Severity: WARNING
  • Description: useEffect or useCallback missing referenced closure variables in dependency array.
  • Remediation: Include all referenced variables in the dependency array or wrap in useCallback.

docs.title: 15.2 RCT-002: Conditional Hook Call
docs.text:
• Default Severity: ERROR
  • Description: React hook invoked conditionally inside if-statement or loop.
  • Remediation: Move hook calls to the top level of the component function.

docs.title: 15.3 RCT-003: Direct State Mutation
docs.text:
• Default Severity: ERROR
  • Description: Mutating state directly (state.val = 1) rather than using state dispatcher.
  • Remediation: Use setState dispatcher or produce an immutable copy.

docs.title: 15.4 RCT-004: Missing Key in List
docs.text:
• Default Severity: WARNING
  • Description: JSX element inside .map() loop is missing a unique key prop.
  • Remediation: Provide a stable unique identifier as the key prop: <Item key={item.id} />.

docs.title: 15.5 RCT-005: Barrel Import Bloat
docs.text:
• Default Severity: WARNING
  • Description: Importing from root barrel file causing excessive bundle size.
  • Remediation: Import from specific subpaths (e.g. '@mui/material/Button').

docs.title: 16.1 NXT-001: Server Component Client API
docs.text:
• Default Severity: ERROR
  • Description: Client hooks or browser globals used in Server Component without 'use client'.
  • Remediation: Add 'use client' directive to the top of the file or extract client logic into a separate component.

docs.title: 16.2 NXT-002: Client Component Private Secret
docs.text:
• Default Severity: CRITICAL
  • Description: Client component references server-only environment variable.
  • Remediation: Prefix variable with NEXT_PUBLIC_ if intended for browser, or access only on server.

docs.title: 1. Overview & Security Philosophy
docs.text: StackVet is designed to operate safely on untrusted repositories, including open-source pull requests, third-party codebases, and continuous integration pipelines. StackVet adheres to the principle of least privilege, strict defense in depth, and zero arbitrary code execution.

docs.title: 2. Security Trust Boundaries
docs.text:
┌────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│                   Untrusted Input                      │
│  - Repository file trees                               │
│  - Manifests (pyproject.toml, package.json, lockfiles) │
│  - Git diff hunks & commit metadata                    │
│  - Symlinks & file paths                               │
└──────────────────────────┬─────────────────────────────┘
                           │ Strict Boundary Enforcement
┌──────────────────────────▼─────────────────────────────┐
│                 StackVet Core Engine                   │
│  - Safe AST-only parsers (ruff-python, oxc)            │
│  - Canonical root boundary containment                 │
│  - Resource limits (size, depth, file count)           │
│  - Format-preserving atomic remediation                │
└──────────────────────────┬─────────────────────────────┘
                           │ Sanitized Diagnostics & Exit Codes
┌──────────────────────────▼─────────────────────────────┐
│                   Verified Outputs                     │
│  - SARIF v2.1.0 / JSON / Text reports                  │
│  - Standardized exit codes (0, 1, 2, 3, 4)             │
│  - Zero secret or token leakage in error messages      │
└────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘

docs.title: 3.1 Zero Arbitrary Code Execution
docs.text:
• Static Analysis Only: StackVet never invokes Python interpreters (python, python3), Node runtimes (node), package managers (pip, npm, pnpm), or shell subprocesses during repository analysis.
  • Pure Rust AST Parsers: All code parsing is performed using memory-safe Rust implementations:
  • Python AST: ruff_python_parser and ruff_python_ast
  • JavaScript / TypeScript AST: oxc_parser and oxc_ast
  • TOML / JSON / YAML: toml, toml_edit, serde_json, and serde_yaml
  • Execution of arbitrary code or untrusted configuration scripts is impossible by architecture.

docs.title: 3.2 Canonical Repository Boundary Enforcement & Symlink Containment
docs.text:
• Path Traversal Defense: All file paths derived from git diffs, command-line arguments, or repository file trees are validated against the canonical repository root: 
    canonical_candidate.starts_with(&canonical_root)
    Any path containing path traversal attempts (such as ../../etc/passwd or outside absolute paths) is rejected and excluded from scanning.
  • Symlink Protection:
  • By default, symlinks pointing outside the repository root or cyclical symlinks are ignored.
  • Skipped symlinks are recorded in scan results and surfaced as diagnostic DISC-005 ("Scan resource limit or repository boundary exceeded").

docs.title: 3.3 Resource Exhaustion & Denial of Service Protection
docs.text:
To prevent algorithmic complexity attacks or memory exhaustion on malicious or oversized repositories, StackVet enforces configurable resource limits:

Limit Default Configuration (stackvet.toml) Diagnostic Emitted Max File Size 10 MB (10,485,760 bytes) [scanner] max_file_size DISC-005 Max Traversal Depth 40 directory levels [scanner] max_depth Stopped silently Max Scanned Files 50,000 files [scanner] max_files DISC-005 (is_truncated) Symlink Following false [scanner] follow_symlinks DISC-005

Files exceeding the file size limit are excluded from in-memory AST generation to prevent OOM panics.

docs.title: 3.4 Secret Leakage Prevention in Diagnostic Messages
docs.text:
• Parser errors from malformed manifests or syntax errors (DISC-001 through DISC-004) only disclose file location, line/column coordinates, and concise parser state descriptions.
  • File contents, raw token streams, or potential credentials (e.g. SECRET_KEY = "...") are never echoed into diagnostic messages or reports.

docs.title: 4. Incomplete Analysis vs. Clean Scans
docs.text:
When scanning untrusted repositories, an analysis may be partial if: 1. Manifests are corrupted or unreadable (DISC-001, DISC-004). 2. Source files contain invalid syntax (DISC-002, DISC-003). 3. Repository boundaries or resource limits are exceeded (DISC-005).

To prevent false confidence where an incomplete analysis reports zero security findings: - ReportSummary tracks is_complete: bool and incomplete_reasons: Vec<String>. - In CI pipelines, --fail-on-incomplete or scanner.fail_on_incomplete = true causes StackVet to exit with Exit Code 4 (IncompleteAnalysis).

docs.title: 5. Standard Process Exit Codes
docs.text: Code Name Description 0 Success Command succeeded; no findings at or above configured thresholds. 1 FindingsViolation Findings detected that violate configured severity thresholds or baseline regressions. 2 ConfigurationError Invalid configuration syntax, unrecognized rule ID, or unsupported severity override. 3 ExecutionError Operational I/O error (e.g. missing target path or unreadable baseline file). 4 IncompleteAnalysis Analysis could not be fully completed due to malformed files, unreadable files, or resource limit exhaustion when --fail-on-incomplete is requested.

docs.title: Dependency & Architecture Tree
docs.text: stackvet provides visual representations of both your package dependency tree and your internal source module import architecture.

docs.title: 1. Basic Usage
docs.text:
# Render full project view (dependencies + import graph)
stackvet graph

# Alias for stackvet graph
stackvet graph

docs.title: 2. Visualizing Package Dependencies
docs.text:
To focus exclusively on direct and transitive package dependencies:

stackvet graph --dependencies
# or shorthand:
stackvet graph -d

docs.title: 2.1 Limiting Tree Depth
docs.text:
Limit the hierarchy depth using --depth / -L:

stackvet graph -d -L 2

Example output:

Dependency Hierarchy

fastapi (0.110.0) [direct]
├── starlette (0.36.3) [transitive]
│   └── anyio (4.3.0) [transitive]
│       └── idna (3.6) [transitive]
└── pydantic (2.6.4) [direct]
    ├── annotated-types (0.6.0) [transitive]
    └── pydantic-core (2.16.3) [transitive]

docs.title: 3. Visualizing Internal Module Imports & Circular Loops
docs.text:
To inspect internal Python module imports and pinpoint circular dependency cycles:

stackvet graph --imports
# or shorthand:
stackvet graph -i

Example output:

Internal Module Import Architecture

services.payment
├── models.transaction
└── core.config

services.auth
├── utils.security
└── [🔴 CIRCULAR CYCLE] services.payment -> services.auth

docs.title: 4. Dependency Risk Graph (stackvet dependency --graph / stackvet graph --risk)
docs.text:
Take dependency trees further by analyzing usage patterns, functional classifications, and diagnostic risk levels across direct and transitive dependencies:

# Render annotated dependency risk graph
stackvet dependency --graph

# Or via tree with risk flag
stackvet graph --risk

docs.title: 4.1 Node Annotations & Classification
docs.text:
The Dependency Risk Graph classifies each package into its ecosystem role: - Framework Core: e.g., fastapi, celery, django, sqlalchemy, flask - Runtime Driver / Infrastructure: e.g., amqp, kombu, asyncpg, psycopg2, redis, uvicorn - Application Library: e.g., requests, httpx, pydantic, rich - Dev & Tooling: e.g., pytest, ruff, mypy, black

Example Output: 

🛡️  Dependency Risk Graph: payment-service (3 direct, 48 total packages)
└── Production Dependencies
    └── celery v5.4.0 (>=5.3.0)  HEALTHY
        ├── Type: Direct dependency
        ├── Import: Directly imported (4 files)
        ├── Role: Framework core
        ├── Assessment: No diagnostic issues found; dependency is healthy
        └── kombu v5.3.5  HEALTHY
            └── amqp v5.2.0  INFORMATIONAL
                ├── Type: Transitive dependency
                ├── Import: No direct AST import found
                ├── Role: Runtime driver / message broker
                └── Assessment: Safe runtime dependency (DEP-003 informational)

docs.title: 4.2 Filtering by Risk Level
docs.text:
Filter the dependency graph by risk threshold: 

# Show only high and critical risk dependencies
stackvet dependency --graph --risk high

# Show only healthy packages
stackvet dependency --graph --risk healthy

docs.title: 4.3 Compact Mode & JSON Export
docs.text:
# Render risk tree without detailed multi-line annotations
stackvet dependency --graph --no-annotate

# Export full risk graph metadata as JSON
stackvet dependency --graph --json

docs.title: 5. JSON Export for Tooling
docs.text:
To emit the tree hierarchy, package statistics, and detected cycles as structured JSON for CI ingestion or custom dashboards:

stackvet graph --json > graph.json

docs.title: ARC-001: Architecture layer violation
docs.text: Attribute Value Rule ID ARC-001 Category architecture Default Severity WARNING

docs.title: Description
docs.text: A module in an upper architectural layer directly imports a lower layer bypassing intermediate abstraction layers, or a lower layer imports an upper layer.

docs.title: Why This Matters
docs.text: Detecting and addressing architecture layer violation prevents runtime failures, dependency conflicts, or configuration drift in production environments.

docs.title: Remediation
docs.text: Route access through intermediate service/repository layers or invert the dependency using interfaces.

docs.title: Configuration & Suppression
docs.text:
To suppress this rule for a specific file or line, add an inline comment:

# stackvet:ignore ARC-001

Or configure a rule override in .stackvet.toml:

[rules]
"ARC-001" = "off" # or "warning", "error"

docs.text: Attribute Value Rule ID ARC-002 Category architecture Default Severity ERROR

docs.title: Description

docs.title: Remediation
